sections.h:
Wednesday

TC pp. 39-40, «Discernment of faith… or rather, theology of history»

Discernment of faith among so many deceptive roads.

Rosa Gattorno is convinced, also from her own experience, that «man's life is a hard toil» (Job 7:1), a constant struggle between good and evil; that in the kingdom of God, for whose growth one works, it is difficult to distinguish the good wheat from the weeds; that a true instinct of faith is needed to find, among so many confusing roads, often so alluring and specious, the one that leads to Him who is the true Way: the supreme Good. This is what we may call the philosophy of the poem Travails and Comforts: a panoramic view of the history of salvation, whose fabric is woven both from the personal travail of her spirit, amid alternations of light and darkness, of consolation and dryness, and from the arduous task of the foundress, engaged day and night in protecting the «workers» of the Work of God, entrusted to her, against so many false guides, and in making of them courageous cultivators of the fields of the Lord. One may say that in every episode this philosophy, or rather theology of history, is symbolized.

Thursday

TC pp. 457-458, «Only from the Cross… the workers who came looking for me»

Thus weary I fell asleep leaning against a tree trunk, which served me as a pillow. I slept deeply. A voice from afar woke me, calling me by name, that I might go to the aid of people who were sure of their purpose, namely that from the beatings I had received I would no longer be able to move. But, once awake, I found myself full of vigor. My voice:

- Run to the people who want to plot against my fields; and do not stop until you have an order from me.

Full of vigor I rose and, running, reached the field. Set to work, the field gained strength and so all heard that I was approaching them. They were frightened and sought to collect themselves. The workers worked the ground with alacrity. God let me see, through one of the workers, how beautiful the great field of his Work had become. My voice:

- It is not time to stop, but rather to run along this narrow path to arrive where your Master awaits you.

- Oh! - I exclaimed - I will not stop any more and always, day and night, I will try to walk so as to arrive and see my Beloved!

- Your eagerness is most pleasing; but it is not thus that I want it. Take care! for much of the time you must remain on this path.

Alas! I stopped. Is there then no middle way?

Weary in mind and in continual anxiety, I fell asleep. Awakened, I found myself in a pleasant field, but through the keeper's inertia a great deal of weeds was springing up in it. A good shepherd was advising the workers to come looking for me.

Friday

FS p. 23, «And she knew how to instill… we shall be at rest for an eternity»

And she knew how to instill courage in her collaborators, in the superiors, in individual sisters and in other persons who confided in her. There is hardly a letter of hers in which the word does not leap out: Courage! Here are some of the words of encouragement that we find in her letters to the sisters, amid vibrant expressions of affection:

«My dear child, come, courage!» - «Be of good heart, for heaven is favorable to you!» - «Courage, my dear! let us work, for afterward we shall rest blessed. Be strong, do not fear!» - «Patience, my dear, courage!… courage!» - «My beloved ones, courage, for one day you will see your God and will enjoy your labors» - «Courage, and all confidence in the good God!» - «Courage, for in the moment of trial courage and patience are needed, peace and resignation. With this everything is obtained and every obstacle is overcome» - «Courage! If the road is closed on every side, we must go forward by dint of sweating blood, until we have a drop of it left in our veins!» - «First commend yourself to God, and then forward with courage!» - «Courage, my daughter! for one day we shall taste the fruit of the blood and sweat shed in our labors!» - «Courage, forward! for one day we shall be at rest for an eternity!».

Saturday

TC pp. 73-74, «A great ship that… and the others took part»

After a few hours' walk I arrived at a shore and saw no sign any more, only sea. I turned my gaze to both sides to see if there were any tracks, but nothing: only an immense beach with soft sand. The murmur of the sea, the scorching sun, caused me great fright. Prostrate I began to weep, like one waiting for what she was to do. After a long prayer:

- My Good! - I exclaimed - My Savior! Oh! how happy I would be if I too, as you made Peter walk on the sea (cf. Mt 14:29-31), had such a fate! Oh! trace a way across the sea as well so that I may run!

But nothing! A great wind rises and the sea is more agitated than ever and all at once becomes frightening. From afar something could be seen. As a wave lifts and hurls closer a great ship that was about to be wrecked. On the sides certain monsters in the form of fish could be seen, trying to sink it and plunge it into that abyss. At such a sight I threw myself to the ground and, with all the voice I had, cried for help. The work of the monsters grew stronger and the ship at every instant seemed to me submerged. Weeping I called my God, almost fainting from grief and fright; my Savior comes near me:

- Why doubt! - he said to me - the ship is mine and cannot sink.

I remained in ecstasy, and all grew calm on the sea. The sky was clear and the ship, under full sail, was nearing the port. Turning to my Good: - I am exhausted of strength! - I exclaimed.

The fright, the grief that it would be destroyed, made me die!

What? have you forgotten my promises? - he said to me.

Taking me by the hand, he made me climb onto the ship; and my Good disappeared. Wholly strengthened and full of courage, I ran everywhere to see what was needed and asked everyone what they required. I noticed that something was lacking, namely the helmsman. The captain was disturbed, in all the passengers reigned the greatest anguish. At my first conversation with the commander I received an insult:

- How can we go on, if we have no one to put at the helm? Why, when we were on land, did you not let me go ashore and provide for myself?

As if I had been the cause, he grew ever more furious, and the others took part.

4th Sunday of Ordinary Time

TC pp. 425-426, «Faith governed me and I was sure of… how am I to shed them?»

Faith governed me and I was sure of managing to remove that mountain and reduce it as my Master had told me. The workers, frightened and fearing that I would order them to help me, asked me to go and work elsewhere, because they felt that this work would bring them down and they would not hold out. I looked at them and, patience! Exclaiming thus, I gave them leave to go where the ground was prepared for sowing.

Seeing myself alone on that mountain working, the more I toiled to bring it down the more I saw I had done nothing. What pain I felt! Thus dejected, my mind was already becoming troubled with the thought of having been an illusion and that there might be diabolical art. I stopped to think: My God! how to transport all this material?

Weary, exhausted, I rested and laid my head on a stone. I fell asleep amid sobs. Behold once more my Savior who, taking me by the hand, made me climb to the top of this mountain, and in the midst of its veins blood was flowing. I was frightened and asked him what this was: - It is your blood! and only with this will this mountain become a beautiful and delightful plain. Many people will come to drink the water that will spring from a fountain. Many zealous workers will come to help you. But first, you must form all those streams that you have seen.

And he goes away! Awakened: where am I? where is my Good? Yes, it was He, for I feel that he has left his grace in me. What mystery is this? Fool that I am: it is not that this mountain is to be brought down by toil, but now I understand well: by suffering! My God, those streams of blood, how am I to shed them?

Monday

FS pp. 160-161, «How to accept sufferings and make them fruitful… remember that new days bring new crosses»

How to accept sufferings and make them fruitful?

Here, as in other aspects of her evangelical pedagogy, Mother Rosa shows herself an outstanding spiritual guide of the souls entrusted to her. It is impossible to transcribe the whole variety of her recommendations on the way to sanctify suffering, each of which almost always opens with that Courage! of hers, so maternal in tone. A useful anthology of the spirituality of suffering could be assembled.

As an expert in what she teaches, she often alludes to her own sufferings - physical ailments, struggles, setbacks - as if she wished to give heart through the sharing of such a gift of God. She often says to the sister she sees suffering: «I wish I could ease you by taking all your suffering upon myself». She teaches them to give reasons, first of all, for accepting sufferings: «Jesus gave all his blood for us, and we must do likewise: yes, blood for blood!» (Letter to Sr. A. Carlotta Biagini: 10/19/1873). She then teaches them to know how to discover the loving hand of God in sufferings and also to feel the caress of the same hand that sends or permits the affliction. God, in fact, soothes our wounds and sweetens our pain (Letter to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni: 4/5/1871, 2/5/1872).

«My dear, when that blessed hand of the eternal Father strikes us, ah! how sweet are his blows! Yes, my dear: I would do nothing but kiss it and clasp it!» (Letter to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni: 4/14/1869; cf. Letter to Sr. Francesca Camisa: 12/16/1868, 8/17/1870).

The important point, and not an easy one, is to keep interior peace and joy of heart unaltered under the weight of the cross (Letter to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 1867, 5/26/1873). To succeed in this disposition one needs a good dose of patience and much faith:

«Come, courage! Soon you will see that the Lord will console you; but an ounce of patience and two of faith in God, and you will have everything, I assure you. But peace, and little sophistry; day by day embrace the cross that the Lord sends us; remember that new days bring new crosses» (Letter to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 8/12/1870).

Tuesday

FS pp. 166-167, «A few days after… to obey him: what do you think?»

A few days after the date of this letter she set out on a long journey through France. Certainly, very often her dear Good came to her aid even in miraculous form. Just as she obtained healing for her sick daughters - there are many cases attested in the processes, - so she confidently asked, for herself too, for the remedy when she knew that otherwise she could not be useful to the Institute. At the beginning of 1889 she had a serious swelling in a leg; informing D. Gennaro, she said to him:

«May it always be as pleases my God. He sent it to me: in everything fully resigned and calm, cheerful, as if this donkey were carrying nothing, though this morning it would not stand straight at all, I kept feeling faint; but now I am a little better. May my Jesus do what pleases him: always happy to be able to suffer!».

And, thinking of so many in the world who must bear even more painful sufferings, she ends with one of her fine outbursts of love: «I would like to be able to absorb all the sufferings of the world, if it should please my sovereign Lord!» (1/24/1889).

A few weeks later she was almost certain of having obtained the grace of improvement:

«I threw myself at the feet of my dear Crucified: My Love, you sent it to me, and you will see to it» (Feb. 1889). But at the end of that year she felt very ill: «I saw it was bad! - she writes - It is little for my sins!». Which did not prevent her from setting out for southern Italy. She found relief by repeating: «It is sweet to suffer for Jesus!» (1/25/1890). With the princess of Fitalia she complained because she now felt obliged to take care of her body: «It no longer wants to obey: once I commanded it, now it has found the means of making itself obeyed: what do you think?» (9/26/1889).

Wednesday

FS pp. 24-25 «This, which we might call the pedagogy… who will be against us?»

This, which we might call the pedagogy of courage, appears in a special way in the correspondence with the princess of Fitalia, her spiritual daughter, sorely tried by dryness and other sufferings. She repeats to her:

«Courage, for in the time of trial much is gained!» - «Oh! I can well call you by the title of gracious and strong, of resolute spirit, noble warrior, always victorious in your undertakings» - «Courage in your undertaking! the work you are doing is pleasing to God…, courage!» - «Courage, never be dismayed; Jesus is with you, who can prevail against you?» - «Courage; let us press upon the Heart of Jesus, he will console us» (Letter of 6/26/1885, 1/15/1886, 7/20/1893, 9/2/1893, 11/2/1893, 2/27/1895).

In the catalog of the virtues there is one that is linked to fortitude, a virtue and gift of the Holy Spirit, and is called magnanimity and also boldness: it helps to overcome faintheartedness in the face of obstacles to be overcome. In a note to Msgr. Granito di Belmonte Mother Rosa wrote:

«A line in haste, to give you good news: I have made the contract for the schools (in Naples), and they are already working. Long live boldness! What do you say? It is not boldness, but only trust in my God» (Letter of 9/22/1896).

Here is the secret of that energy of character which aroused admiration: Mother Rosa was a woman of faith; she was sure that, in her own weaknesses, she could always count on the strength of God: I can do all things in him who strengthens me (Phil 4:13). And she was convinced she had God on her side, since the Institute founded by her was the Work of the Lord; so in her writings the well-known text of Saint Paul leaps out now and then: If God is for us, who can be against us? (Rom 8:31).

Thursday

FS pp. 149-150, «As I stopped, my Crucified… to fly to the supreme Good»

As I stopped, my Crucified placed his heavy cross upon my shoulders and, taking from me the terror of suffering, left me an ardent love for it. I loved it much and I love it greatly» (TC, p. 3-5).

In her first outbursts of love she would have wished to immolate herself radically, all at one stroke, through martyrdom. On March 31, 1862, after a vision of the Host dripping with blood, she had «a most lively, most ardent desire to suffer martyrdom for the faith; and, to be able to give vent to this thought of mine - she writes, - how many things did I not think of to succeed in it! My Good! I would not be satisfied unless I have the fortune to see myself ground to pieces for you, dear Beloved!» (M 1.1, p. 24f).

A year later the same longing returned: to die at the stake as a sign of love and to make satisfaction for sinners; and again in the years 1866 and 1867 (M 1.1, pp. 38, 68, 119; cf. depositions of Sr. A. Fabiana Orsi and Sr. A. Celsa Speranza, Summ., p. 56, 346f).

At last she understood that the slow martyrdom, sustained and renewed day by day, amid bitterness and darkness, was what the divine Crucified asked of her.

On September 17 of that decisive year 1862, her spiritual Father D. Firpo wrote to her:

«The time of consolations, that is, of spiritual delicacies, seems over for you, and from now on you will have only to drink from the bitter chalice of tribulation: it is in tribulation that your lover Jesus wants to unite himself more closely to you; by this sign one recognizes the favorites of God, the predestined, the elect for glory» (cit. by FIOCCHI, I, p. 56).

To live in order to suffer! will be her reply every time the desire for death presents itself to her spirit as the means of freeing herself from the prison of the body and of flying to the supreme Good.

Friday

FS p. 85, «I feel that it is affirmed to me… my

cloud has been far away for some time»

«I feel that it is affirmed to me by my governing Spirit. What a consolation it is for me, who am so abandoned by all human help, to have my dear Spirit, who guides me in everything and sustains me so well!…»

- «Since my director is God, the Being who lives for me, he made me feel how he wanted me to offer him three penances…»

- «A voice said to me: I am your Master, be at peace! The peace of conscience I enjoy is such that I see there is a most powerful Spirit who rules and governs me».

- «How many beautiful things he told me and has taught me, particularly for the Work!… How many caresses when he says to me: My Rosa, courage, for I am with you! do not doubt!»

- «Alone as I find myself…, but it does not confuse me, because all the points are resolved for me one by one by my Jesus. I feel and see myself with more clarity guided by my Spirit. My cloud has been far away for some time…» (M 3, p. 11f, 26; 4.1, p. 4, 6).

Saturday

D. pp. 69-70, par. 4

Infinite Wisdom makes her a sharer in his Light, which penetrates the hearts of men, searches them, shakes them, converts them:

«He let me see into certain hearts and said this to me: every time it is needful for you to see and penetrate them, you will see them. So whatever you ask of me for the good of the souls who are with you and whom you have in your care, I will give you everything. So too for what you desire for Priests, the very thing that with prayer you wish me to give them, I will give them. You will distinguish clearly the good from the bad; I will make you feel a revulsion when they have indecent ideas against chastity. At once you will feel it and you will be warned. Do not doubt that I will always be near you, there are many… Oh! what pain… that I felt. So for the false devout women you will have special lights to distinguish well…» (M. 1.1, p. 63).

She receives most beautiful instructions on the love Jesus has for man, while man responds poorly:

«Oh! my Beloved! Oh! Yes, I see well how much you love creatures, and they respond to you so poorly. You are all love for them! A Voice answered me, yes I love man immensely, and as he said this to me he drew near to me» (M. 1.1, p. 152).

New lights project her toward the future with optimism and hope. She must not fear because there is One who guides her, sustains her and plans for her:

«At night behold he came to console me. He let me see what will happen at my death, what they will do with me, how they will dress me, and who will have ascendancy over it; it will be the one who will have my final direction, who will live by obedience, but will take care not to command me things that he has not first well felt within himself, the habit of a tertiary will be my habit, and the rest Saint Anne's» (M. 11, p. 164).

With the expert guidance of her Master she sees the different aspects of her path in following Christ the Poor One. Jesus shows her gradually, walking with her, how to collaborate in the redemptive work.

He forms her for penitent conversion, for engaging in the struggle with the evil one by dominating him with unconditional faith in her Lord, for being a victim of love in order to create the counterweight in the divine justice provoked by our sins, and for bringing sinners to salvation.

5th Sunday of Ordinary Time

TC pp. 349-351, «It is I who guide your steps… feeling the weight of humanity»

To work with renewed vigor; but one must feel the weight of humanity.

Full of vigor, quite cheerful and as if I had had nothing, I set to work. The workers who were with me looked at me and did not understand how it could be and from where I could have drawn so much strength and vigor. Working, from time to time I thought to myself about what had happened to me and looked at the strength I had. Oh! how your power gives life to the dead!

Meanwhile my mind was (being) enlightened about everything I had to do. I carried out great things with ease and it was curious: when the poor workers saw me so well, they marveled. Within myself I said: they are right, because I too feel I am living another life, so strong.

I set fields and cottages in order. I found much to struggle with among shepherds who had nested in certain farmsteads, what strength it took to make them leave. Their power was great, but the arm of the Lord made them inert for revolt; rather they went away silent, content only to grumble. What work in the Majesty of a God! He makes lambs of lions, subjects them to the judgment of a slave of his, lending weight to her word. The poor creatures, confused, go out and pitch their tents elsewhere.

Such was the work I did that no creature could keep up with me. With the strength of my God, oh! surely no human creature could compete with me, could not! In this way I hurried to put the workers in order and to receive other fields to cultivate.

This strength lasted me a long time, when one fine day, while I was reorganizing a piece of work, I feel my strength failing. I had to sit down on certain tangles of grass, and so silent I watched the work. My voice:

- It is time to resume the work with human strength alone!

What can it mean?

- Speak to me more clearly!

No sooner had I said this than I understood everything: that human nature had to act, and so it was necessary for me to submit to eating and resting. I leaned against a wall and began to weep: My God, why did you withdraw your grace from me and abandon me? Perhaps I did not respond as pleased you? So great was my grief that, rising, I ran to throw myself, where? into a heap of thorn bushes! And I fainted. The sharp thorns pierced my whole body, several remained inside, because they had broken as they went in. But I felt nothing, because I had lost my senses.

My angel Saint Michael took me by the hand and tore me out of that thicket. Once outside, I came to, exhausted. I looked at him. He sat me down and told me not to doubt that I had done everything well and that my God was most pleased with the fulfillment of his will. If he had so ordained, it was nothing other than his good pleasure that I should come to feel again the weight of humanity.

Monday

D. pp. 113-114, par. 1

She experiences the presence of her Beloved in the Cloud from which a voice comes forth that consoles her, reassures her, enlightens her in her doubts:

«Now I consult my cloud. Always, every time I need it, it counsels me, answers me what I must do, how I must conduct myself and I feel comforted in adversity. Oh! last night I saw what beautiful thing was in it» (M. 1.1, p. 85).

In the light of Revelation, the mystical symbol through which the Lord speaks to Rosa to accompany her during the stage of fundamental importance of the foundation becomes clear. Sacred Scripture, which is the reference source for the Church, serves as our guide in studying Rosa's experience of the Cloud.

Exodus offers a full description of the presence of God through the cloud: «The Lord went before them by day in a pillar of cloud to lead them along the way, and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light, that they might travel by day and by night. The pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night did not depart from before the people» (Ex 13:21-22).

Though she finds herself in a historical situation different from the conditions of the pilgrim people of the Exodus, Rosa lives a religious experience of similar spiritual content, aimed at guiding her path in God and that of all those who form the Family that God has entrusted to her:

«…in the midst of so much tumult of an abyss of business, yet I am never deprived of union with my God, indeed for some time, since he supplied me with that dear treasure which I always see at my side and it is a cloud, something beautiful, one sees it contains a being, because as I said above I already saw it…» (M. 1.1, pp. 86-87).

In the verse of the book of Exodus, already cited, one notes how during the long marches in the desert the chosen people was preceded by the Lord with the pillar of cloud.

The testimony of the people who saw the glory of the Lord as a devouring fire in the cloud (cf. Ex 16:10) shows that the cloud is subordinate to the manifestation of the Lord. The cloud makes perceptible the nearness of God the Liberator, Savior, sole Lord of his people.

Tuesday

FS pp. 133-134, «Love and suffering, mission… her banners: suffering and love»

The heart of Rosa Gattorno, a woman's heart, endowed with a rich sensitivity and an exceptional capacity for welcome and affective self-giving, was made to love. And it was also a heart made to suffer. Suffering enters into the Christian logic of oblative and redemptive love, since the love of God for us has been manifested in the fact that he sent his Son as an atoning sacrifice for our sins (1 Jn 4:9f); and the Son of God showed his love for the Father and for men by submitting to the passion and to death on the cross.

It is not only a matter of Mother Rosa's personal spirituality: loving and suffering will also be her destiny as foundress and will constitute her central message to the Daughters of Saint Anne. In the poem Travails and Comforts she presents the growth of the Institute as the laborious rowing of a little boat through the storms of the sea, until, after a great struggle, it is seen coming out victorious unfurling an elegant flag with the inscription: suffering-love. With a favorable sea, the ship, grown very large and well equipped, makes great progress, defends itself successfully against enemies, now strongly armored and girded with iron; it keeps gaining ground, conquers many cities and countries. «Always victorious it makes for great ports and flies its banners: suffering and love» (TC, pp. 219-221).

Wednesday

TC p. 184-187, «The combat grew very fierce… she believes herself abandoned»

The combat grew very fierce. But no! I concluded that I did not need the refreshment of bread, but desired something quite other, for which I languished.

And without more I set myself to run.

It is a scourge - I reasoned with myself - these encounters: in such sad moments humanity complains and finds someone to protect it; the soul fears being importunate and erring in wanting to rule too much over all the faculties; it is confused and begins to fear. What torpor arises from this! Reason is confused, would not want to concede victory to humanity. The demands that humanity in fact shows with the evidence of the lack of its existence, the murmur that still resounds in the ear of the words of the most learned shepherd…: ah! in what straits the soul finds itself! The strength of the spirit, which is always ready to sacrifice everything for the good and salvation of the soul, insists on not heeding, but running without stopping, seeing in humanity something base and trivial.

At last, lack of nourishment overcame me and I fainted. Abandoned on the earth, I commended my soul to God, seized by a strong fear of being deceived and that all this was an effect of illusion. I wept inconsolably. An angel appeared to me - not mine - and said to me:

- Why do you weep? That God who has sustained you until now, will he perhaps not sustain you always?

Having said this, he left me a little basket which had inside a large piece of bread. I set myself quietly to eat: it was exquisite; I devoured it. And I thought how great the goodness of my God! I would have been happier had he satisfied me, not with bread, but with that food of which I feel so ardent a longing to be nourished. Reasoning thus, I see at my feet a crystal clear little spring bubbling up, as if inviting me to drink. Oh! what great wonder I felt! I asked his forgiveness for my fear that what was necessary might fail me. I remained so dejected that I no longer knew how to find words and strength, because everything reproached me. I would have curled up at the bottom of the earth to weep. My grief grew ever greater.

Drowsy in so cruel a state, I lost my senses and remained stretched on the ground. At that moment my angel Saint Michael the Archangel came near and, taking me by the hand, lifted me up; but (I was) so confused and exhausted that I did not recognize him. But the touch of his hand gave me life and, recognizing him, I burst into bitter weeping:

- My wickednesses made me lose my God! I was ungrateful to him; I lacked trust; I complained and desired food… Oh! never again will I ask for bread! I will die of hunger, but I will not complain. I had bread, but not that with which you satisfied me another (time), but bread of men, not of heaven (cf. Jn 6:50f).

And he looked at me with compassion. I sobbed violently; the grief was so strong that I felt my chest opening. When my angel, stretching out his hand, (said to me):

- Enough, weep no more! dry your tears: they have been most pleasing to the Lord. Your imperfections are perfectly canceled. Your God was always near; if he had not sustained you, you would have died of grief; his grace sustained you. If it pleased him to nourish you so, is he not bound to sustain you always with the bread of heavenly nourishment? Come with me!

Strong as a giant I ran, and the consolation I felt erased from my mind any remembrance of what had happened. I asked him a thousand questions: he explained to me how the soul unites with God in sufferings, especially in desolation of spirit; how the more grief it feels at seeing itself abandoned, the more it gains in grace and union with its God, while it believes itself abandoned.

Thursday

D. pp. 103-104, «Rosa too experiences mystically… in the image of Christ and Mary»

Rosa too experiences mystically the Spirit Love, Fire dwelling in her, and bears witness to its modes in the pages of her spiritual memoirs:

«Oh! you are too sweet…; alas, a fire consumes me… it is… as if I held a furnace»;

«For several days the region of the heart seems as if it wanted to open… the fire is burning…»;

«…the fire grew more and more in me so that I could not stand on my feet…»;

«…I thought I would die of the fire; the union with my God devoured me so that I had to distract myself lest they notice…»;

«The fire devoured me, I felt something on the left side as if everything inside me were moving and this most sweet movement, when it comes to me, makes me die…» (M. 1.1, p. 120; M. 12, pp. 31; 46; M. 3, pp. 1; 23).

The gift of the Father, the Holy Spirit, did not exhaust his mission in Mary, burning bush of the definitive theophany, full of grace, in whom with the power of his love he formed Jesus. He has continued to be the Love, the power of the life, mission and resurrection of Jesus, and continues in every person to transmit Trinitarian life and to form in him a child of God.

Within the horizon of this mission of love of his is situated his action toward Rosa, in whom he «dwells», letting himself be experienced mystically as fire and shaping her with this fire in the image of Christ and Mary.

Friday

D. p. 105, «I spent the night… Do not quench the Spirit»

«I spent the night clasped to my Good. Oh! joy! I was dying, so great was the love I felt. Not a single instant did I have outside of him. Eternal my all, who can describe what you do and communicate to the soul and what it experiences in you? Today in you and you for me live. I feel that I have no other life than yours. A calm, an interior peace that I do not know how to describe. I speak, rather I feel… my Spirit. I feel something that is felt and not seen with bodily eyes, but the intellect sees and understands all…» (M. 4.3, p. 16).

It is by this divine power that Rosa bears fruit in the Church and for humanity. Letting herself be shaped by the Spirit, she experiences the blessed consequences of his presence, the fruits of his grace: love and peace: synthesis of joy, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control (Gal 5:22).

The Fire of God - Jesus «will baptize with the Holy Spirit and fire» (Lk 3:16), that Spirit of whom Jesus said: «I have come to bring fire to the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled» (Lk 12:49) - is considered by Christian tradition the symbol, one of the most expressive, of the action of the Holy Spirit. For this reason Paul exhorts Christians saying: «Do not quench the Spirit» (1 Thes 5:19).

Saturday

TC pp. 361-362, «Refreshed and guided by St. Michael… and today you will find the field»

Without caring at all for myself, I went searching to find what my voice had told me. Night falls and still nothing is seen. What, was I deceived? I was weak and felt a fierce need to take food; neither farmsteads nor churches were to be seen. Alone! From exhaustion I began to weep:

- My angel Saint Michael, ah! come to my aid! Leaning against a large tree, I was weeping. In this position I fell asleep. A gentle voice wakes me. Who was it? A heavenly messenger who, in a basket, brought me bread.

- Oh! dear angel! tell me, who sent you?

- God.

- But I - I said with a great sigh - how gladly would I desire to be nourished by him alone!

And I did not dare take the bread. He, with peace, urges me to eat. I took the bread, kissed it and then, kneeling, set myself to eat it. Oh my Love! from you comes this treasure! And then, turning to the messenger, I said to him:

When he sent me this bread, did he bless it? Tell me: what did he tell you to tell me? nothing?

He answered: - That you eat!

- But - I answered - I am not at all satisfied: I want him! And I began to weep, and he comforted me.

When I had finished eating, he gave me water to drink: it was an exquisite liquor. I did not notice that it was night: nothing! The moon was shining brightly. He began to say: - We must set out.

- Well then, will you do me the charity of accompanying me?

He answered:

- Certainly, that is my charge.

I gave a great sigh: Oh my God! you I want, you I want!

He answered:

- Let us hasten our step, for in a few hours you will find him.

So it was. At the first light of dawn, the sound of bells was heard. But on this journey he with sweet discourse instructed me, giving me so much knowledge: how the soul in union with God is blessed, is nourished… Oh! how those hours passed for me! I felt no weariness. Oh! would that the day had never come!

As soon as the church was seen, he vanished. I entered the temple of my God and found myself wholly in him. I asked him whether the voice that sent me on this journey was his command. He answered me:

- Yes! and today you will find the field.

6th Sunday of Ordinary Time

TC p. 52, «My Crucified! I begged him… I meditated on the steps of my Savior»

My Crucified! I begged him and he heard me by placing the cross upon my breast, because I was not worthy to carry it upon my shoulders. My Crucified, upon the breast he placed it very well!

My Crucified! when, face down on the ground, having no more strength from the oppression of grief, I was drowning, he raised me up and nourished me with his love. If my bones bent, my Crucified filled me with the nectar of his love.

Thus walking among cliffs and forests, always on the path marked by his footprints, I did not notice that, all pricked, I was in pain; I felt a giant's strength when I found myself facing people who said to me every sort of insult.

My Crucified! he showed himself beautiful to me and greatly rejoiced in what I suffered; then my love grew toward my persecutors and, if it were not that they offended God, I would have wished their number doubled. I found that they were leading me from Pilate and from the judges; I was ashamed, but in my mind I meditated on the steps of my Savior.

Monday

TC pp. 386-388, «She resumes with new alacrity… the apple of his eye»

My voice:

It is time to sow my fields well.

Provide yourself with good seed and first let the couch grass be removed from the earth.

How shall I do to carry out such a command? I was very pensive, when a seller comes before me, offers me good seed and offers me a large uncultivated field to cultivate. I accepted everything and had to provide the workers. Not finding them, I was distressed; my voice taught me where I should take them and I did not delay in carrying out what was suggested to me; with great activity we worked that field and, after sowing excellent wheat, we gathered a fine and abundant harvest.

We entered other nearby estates and it was a feast at the workers' arrival. But that dragon had carried off some of those who remained there; they were so grieved that no reason was valid to calm them. After a long reasoning they were persuaded and thought no more of what had happened; but they were all intent on repairing the damage those had left, and set vigorously to work so that the weeds should not occupy a better place than the wheat.

I tried to help them with all the strength I had and they, seeing me so weary, abandoned laziness and worked with alacrity. Oh! it is useless for a good captain to order his army to face the enemy and take possession of the ground, if he does not go first, exposing his breast to the grapeshot hurled by the enemy: so an overseer who truly wants her workers to be zealous and wholly intent on the work and always to keep their mind and heart turned to their Lord and Master, must be the first who from dawn to dusk holds the spade in her hand to furrow well all the plots of the earth, so that in order the water of the dear Master's grace may run and water those souls well.

But certain shepherds were so little capable of giving true and sound direction to those dear workers that they gave me much pain and, moreover, they believed they could manage to put me out of the field, so as to overturn once more that fine cultivation which my Father and Master had made. With every sort of invention they tried to slander so as to reach their aim; but it was of no avail. In everything they composed, when they thought they were at last victorious, they were left humiliated: my Master sent a ray of light upon the truth of the facts and their snares remained cast down. How many times I felt great compassion, knowing that they were not striking the slave, but touching the Work of God, which is the apple of his eye!

Tuesday

TC pp. 402-403, «Your ignorance… and so magnificently ordered»

Alone, with slow steps, I made my way toward a field where I knew there was great work to be done. As I walked thus pensive, halfway I met a good shepherd, and on drawing near him I sensed something supernatural.

Oh! I am not mistaken, this is a servant of yours, my God! And at once I asked him how he was and where he was headed. With all courtesy and charity he answered me that he was going in search of a person from whom he expected great good for a little flock of his.

I accompanied him, speaking much of my God. Drawing near to a cottage, which was inhabited by my workers, I tried to take leave in order to enter; but he stops me, telling me that the one he was seeking was I.

- Oh! can it be? I am a poor slave of the Lord who knows nothing but to dig the ground and go where my Master commands me.

But he insisted. My voice:

- Listen to him and give him lodging, for a fine estate he will join to my others.

I welcomed him and, having given him as best I could a little room to lie down, we parted with the words:

- Tomorrow everything will be arranged. And he was quite enthusiastic; it would take too much to narrate his protestations and how much he blessed the Lord for having at last made him find the one he had been seeking for many years.

He having withdrawn, I went to my God and begged him much to give me clear understanding to treat so important a matter well:

- Oh my Love! your slave is very ignorant.

My voice:

- To your ignorance my wisdom will make up!

I fell silent, and without more set myself to the work, not caring what I would say, what I would do and what would happen. How the work turned out for me! The arrangements and interweavings were magnificent things. When it was finished, I did nothing but gaze upon the divine ordering; I delighted in what I saw so beautiful and so magnificently ordered.

Wednesday

TC pp. 521-523, «Always forward, without… God gave you great knowledge»

Against the expectation of all the workers, I set out and at the first farmstead where I stopped, after a long journey, I began to have great struggles, because countless were the people who tried to dissuade me, making me observe that such a road was entrenched by evildoers; every sort of frightening tale they tried to tell me. But no! I clung to the feet of my Crucified and asked him what I should do.

- Forward! - he answered me - Do not fear! So I arrived at another farmstead. Snow fell in big flakes, the cold was something horrible; those great valleys and the very high mountains were all covered with snow. At every step, a poor man with a donkey who helped each other, I would say, because now one fell and now the other: they tried to get near certain farmhouses that could scarcely be made out, being covered with snow. It was picturesque!

After having covered many leagues, whenever I came upon someone, they at once urged me to turn back, because that road was most dangerous and it was not fitting for a creature to venture on it; and when they saw my obstinacy, they tried to seduce the workers who were with me. Arrived at a certain point, I truly came to see certain evildoers who were getting ready to start a brawl and it was clearly understood that they had great desire for blood. Seized with fright, a thousand thoughts crossed my mind: the fear that the workers I had with me would fail me from fright, and how much a mind upset by such horrible sights witnessed, and by fancies, can create. I felt inclined to stop. I began to pray:

- My Master! must I stop? How can it be that this is your will: that I go further in, while with every step I advance the evildoers increase? Oh! shall I stop?

As I said this, a dear soul of mine, who dwells in the heavenly homeland, appeared and said to me:

- Do not fear: forward! Nothing sinister will happen to you. I will always be with you.

Full of vigor, encouraged by so great a saint, I ran swiftly on my path and, crossing most numerous fields and sea, at last I happily arrived where my Lord had commanded me.

How can I express the joy of the workers who came to meet me? Among the many there was one whose (appearance) stood out in a singular way. Who was she? A great lady who for years has been working in the fields of the Lord in an extraordinary way: my beloved, tireless for the greater glory of God. She, invested with a sublime spirit, as always was a great relief to me in everything! What a matron, distinguished for her noble qualities, always keeping so charitable a heart and an upright and sincere spirit. Oh! sublime woman, who thinks only of relieving the wretched! This slave, generously benefited by you, beholds your merits and your great virtues. God gave you great knowledge!

Thursday

TC pp. 523-524, «Symbolic vision… he gave me a look and everything vanished»

Sad I moved my steps, seized by the thought that on this earth nothing was worthy of a God. Why this deep thought? Is it not You, O Creator, who took pleasure in creating everything that exists?

I raise my eyes to heaven: what do I see? Seven tablets reddened with blood, which seemed supported by streaks of fire; a most beautiful angel, much resembling Saint Michael, with a long vine-shoot supported them. From afar, Peter, head of the Church, who was praying, looking at the tablets grew gloomy, and wept. A legion of angels, who were singing a sorrowful song, accompanied with their instruments. Everything was sorrowful.

All stop. In a great and infinite space, almost dark, beautiful souls clothed in mourning were seen. Here and there black drapes were seen. An infinity of people: they stood indifferent, as if they were incapable of understanding anything. Every now and then a loud groan came forth: from where? - I said to myself - I look at Saint Peter: it was not he who sent forth such a lament: no! What a lament! it was heart-rending. I asked the angel to explain to me what it meant. He answered me:

- It is the Church that suffers!

- The tablets that you hold up, what do they mean?

- I cannot tell you.

He let me see a horrible thing, and said to me:

- This is a most acute pain that the Church suffers.

At that sight I felt I would die: such was the fright. It was the indifference of Catholics! It seemed as if each one planted sharp styluses in a Heart. How to make reparation for this? My God! accept this slave of yours who offers herself as a victim in reparation! I felt nothing. Turning to the angel, I said to him:

- Ah! take this sight from me and obtain that God accept me as a victim of expiation.

I would have wished to repair everything, but I could no longer bear that sight. Mercy, my God! I saw nothing more: only the tablets and the angel.

- Tell me, what do they mean? They grew ever redder with blood. The angel gave me a look, and everything vanished.

Friday

TC pp. 193-194, «Gentle and comforting… All fear vanished in me»

Having said this, a great road opens. Carried away by the ardent desire to be able to consume myself wholly in the service of my God, I quickened my pace as much as I could. At the end of it there was a very high and wholly rocky mountain; now and then a bush. My track was marked over rough and cutting stones. At the sight of so steep a way I was frightened; but I was very glad to be able to climb it. I scrambled up with all the strength I had; I tried not to slip.

When I was halfway (up the climb), I found a great cross laid out and, prostrating myself, I prayed. But I felt I could not move. What can it be? Oh! my treasure! I kissed and kissed again that wood, and saw so clearly all that my God had suffered upon it. From weariness and pain in all my limbs I fell asleep with my head resting at the feet of the holy Wood. My voice:

- Awake and take this cross and follow your way.

It was very large; I did not dare put it on my shoulder because I was not worthy. What did I do? I embraced it tightly (saying):

- On my breast you will lie and I will climb Calvary!

So I set out, and sweet to me were the sufferings and pains I felt. And, as if I were near my Savior, I conversed with him. I felt many things that were more than what came from me. I never reached the top: the more road I covered, the more the mountain seemed to rise. Ah! my chest hurt, my knees buckled and my strength could hold no longer. Oh! like my Savior!

The night was dark; the track on this mountain was scarcely marked; I could not even find where to rest this treasure of mine, to which I felt so bound in affection and which I adored with the utmost veneration. What to do? When I looked at the depth of this mountain I was terrified: a single instant of a false move, and I might plunge into that abyss! I began to tremble, when the thought is suggested to me that I had with me the treasure of my Crucified. All fear vanished in me.

Saturday

TC pp. 194-195, «Meanwhile I tried more and more to climb… to satisfy

perfectly the will of my God»

Meanwhile I tried more and more to climb, in the hope of finding a small corner where I could stop, and about this I was thinking:

- Oh! fortunate apostles who, before Calvary, saw and enjoyed the delights of Tabor, and saw my God beautiful in all his infinite majesty!

At last I found a small stretch of ground and thought of stopping to take strength and spend the night there. One pain I had: I did not know how to place the cross. What did I do? I spread out my habit and then laid it upon it with all delicacy.

Oh! how beautiful you are! you served as last bed to my God who expired upon you! But how shall I ever carry you on my breast as you deserve? My voice:

- Upon it take your rest: you will gain strength to walk.

I did not hesitate a moment and lay down upon the cross. Oh! gentle and sweet repose! what contentment I felt! I fell asleep, if sleep it can be called, because I learned the most beautiful lessons of mysticism; I formed a conversation and had the most beautiful answers even on cases of conscience. How well he explained to me his law and that of the Church, the parables of the holy Gospel!

At last, awakening late in the morning:

- What? am I alone? Where is the one with whom I was conversing until now?

I looked around: I am truly alone! Strengthened and as if I had come from a hearty meal, I rose and knelt to make a little adoration to the holy Wood. But everything I had heard was always before my mind. My voice:

- Take your cross and walk!

I placed it on my breast and continued to climb. How rocky and very disastrous the way was! But I felt nothing. Every now and then I kissed my companion, pressed her to my breast and repeated to her everything I had learned in the night and which had so comforted me that it seemed I had no further need of anything else: only to try to satisfy perfectly the will of my God.

7th Sunday of Ordinary Time

TC pp. 199-201, «You will learn not to flee from suffering… your path be taken away»

«You will learn not to flee from suffering and not to let yourself be overcome by fear».

Oh! how? who can it have been? The cross was taken from my breast and I was freed also from the molestation of the beasts. Recovered, I looked around; I looked for my cross, and nothing! nor the beasts either! Freed from such fierce molestations, I set out in search of my cross. My voice:

- Do not worry: run along the path!

Doing so and thinking of that sweet moment I had spent with my God, I did not notice where and how the road was; but I reasoned within myself: suffering is very sweet! when two evildoers who were dressed as shepherds stop me.

«Stop!» they said to me.

«No!»

And frightened more than ever I set myself to run with all the strength I had; they too ran, but outside of my path; they shouted because they could never reach me. Finally, arrived at the top of a precipice, (I thought): surely, they will catch me, because I will never throw myself down to save myself. When they were about to come near, my angel took me by the hand and down into that depth made me descend without my noticing. Oh! how I thanked him! I prostrated myself on the ground and begged him to remain with me, for in that valley, surely, there would be nothing but savages; and I was even more afraid of the evildoers than of the tigers. He listened to me, and then lowered his gaze (and said to me):

«Do not fear!».

And he vanished. Alone on that stony road, for nearby the river ran agitated!… Every now and then the laments of little birds were heard, as if they wished to announce to me the approach of some storm. What fright! I ran, and never found either a hut or a creature. Where will I end up? I said to myself. Ever uglier were the two mountains on the sides, one all caves, the other so ill-formed, made of bushes and brambles, full of great trees that could be felt to be inhabited by little birds; in short, it was a terror.

Tightly I held my crucifix to my breast and walked. Finally I see in the distance a little old woman who carried on her poor shoulders a quantity of firewood. Moved to compassion, I hastened my step. When I reached her, I begged her to give me that wood, that I would carry it to wherever she wished. The good woman gladly gave it to me. But the evil one, or rather my own wickedness, put it into my head that by doing this charity to this poor woman, she would be obliged to lodge me, and so I would get out of this terrible road.

Without further thought, I go and, arrived at the poor woman's hut, I set down the wood; and she tries to thank me and invites me to rest that night in her cottage. And I gladly accept. My God! what did I do? While going with her I strayed from the path and the farmstead was full of people who were blaspheming!

I leave in haste and no longer see my path. Where am I? I began to weep, far away from that horrid cottage, asking my God's pardon if I had failed in this; if I did it, it was to relieve that poor woman and so do an act of charity.

«Ah! no!» my angry voice «the double aim has taken from you all the merit and the avoidance of suffering: lack of faith and of trust in God! Thus you have given occasion for your rightful path to be taken away.

Monday

TC p. 479, «Rise and pray… How great your goodness, my Lord!»

Rise and pray: the rest you have taken is enough!

Rising at once, I began to pray. Only two hours had passed when I heard a knock at the door. I asked who it was and what was wanted; the maidservant answered, telling me that the lady wanted me with her. I made my way through such beautiful rooms, all elegantly adorned, and finally arrived in her room. She lay in bed; I thought the hour for going to church was near, when she has me come close to her bed and asks my pardon because it was not yet three o'clock and she had had me awakened. The maidservant answers that I had not yet gone to sleep; but with persuasive manner and words I tried to assure the lady that I had already slept enough and begged her to be at ease on my account and to tell me what she desired. She sent the woman away and, putting her hands around my neck, said to me:

- Ah! do not abandon me! I greatly desire to love God, but there is one thing that prevents me.

I encouraged her and, in the end, she revealed the secret to me and, set on the right way, assured me that she would do everything I had told her. She burst into bitter weeping and said:

- You have saved me!

She came with me to church and, finally, made her holy Communion after a well-made confession. Oh! how much I prayed that she might resolve! How great your goodness, my Lord!

Tuesday

TC pp. 257-258, «On the rough path with my feet… to be shed upon these stones»

- Conversion of a group of women who then follow her.

Without further thought I set out. It was a road full of stones and ascents and descents and dry torrent beds. In short, it was a painful way; my feet were already all wounded and I kept them very swollen. I did not dare utter a word of complaint, indeed I felt great satisfaction. I suffered greatly, but the taste of so fierce an anguish was a sweet consolation to me; and I tried to run more and more. Already blood was coming from my feet.

Oh! how I consoled myself thinking of my Savior who, on the return from Egypt, barefoot, ran ahead of the most holy Virgin and Saint Joseph, and that these two persons felt great pain, especially when they saw that blood came from the divine soles. Oh! how they were seized with great apprehension and offered to carry him, but He would not consent and continued on his way. Oh! how sweet and very consoling it is to me to think that this wretched blood had the fortune to be shed upon these stones!

Wednesday

TC pp. 227-230, «Everything that is not of God… assures you a blessedness»

Awakened by a sweet call, like Samuel (cf. 1 Sam 3:4-10), I answered:

«Here I am, my Lord, ready to fulfill your most holy will!

But what a marvel! I no longer found myself (where I had been before). I turned and turned again my gaze: I saw nothing but graceful groups of peasant girls who were working the earth and cheerfully sang the praises of Mary. And beautiful was their work: of every sort of fruit and flower and more there was. Oh! how well worked it is! I drew near and, with all kindness, they asked me who I was and how I found myself in that field of theirs, where no living creature has ever entered.

«And you are alone? Why do you not answer our questions?» they said.

«You are right, good young women: forgive me. I am a poor slave of my Lord and here He himself has brought me.

They answered:

«Who is this master of yours?»

«What, do you not know him?»

«No!»

«Do you not know God?»

«We have never heard him named.»

«But you are joking! I do not believe it.»

They rose from their work.

«We tell you that we know nothing!

«But tell me, please: who do you believe made these beautiful fruits grow, if not my Lord? It is He who, with his grace, has made all these delightful plants grow.

They began to tease me and to tell me that they have a master who is very skilled and knows agriculture very well, and that they work for him.

«So you work for man and not for God? Everything that is not of God is consumed on the earth.

One of them looked at me attentively, and said to me:

«Teach me these beautiful things! I feel within my heart a force that drives me to come with you.

Had she never said it! The others all (began) to shriek and wanted to make themselves heard by the master, that he might not allow it. But the young woman, nimble, leaps over a bush and gets out.

«Oh! if you others too would follow me, it would be very good: what great things you would understand!

But there was no chance. Only one! and with her I continued my journey. And sweetly I taught her. How blessed I was! Only that I thought of those poor creatures I had left behind. She looked at me and said to me: «Why are you so pensive?»

«When I think of those who remained I feel a terrible stab.»

«Let us go back» she said to me «and you will tell them what you have told me. Surely they will come.

My voice:

«Forward! or else you will lose this one too.»

«No!» I said to her «the Lord will take care of those.»

Having said this I noticed that she thought she had done wrong and was hesitant to return; when a voice was heard that called us loudly. She, turning, said to me:

«It is those companions of mine who beg us to wait for them.

My voice:

«Stop!»

These poor creatures came, telling me that the master had driven them off rudely. I welcomed them all, and began to make them know how the world pays and that only God gives the just reward and never abandons.

«Yes, what I tell you is the truth, you will experience it: He for an eternity assures you a blessedness.

Thursday

TC pp. 502-503, «Portrait of the model worker… will be doubled for you»

As I ran along this disastrous road, I met the good worker and she, seeing me, told me of many adventures she had been through: the battles she had sustained with certain shepherds who see their own good in a quite curious way.

She is full of spirit and endowed with an uncommon courage, especially when she deals with the affairs of the fields, and something more… She is the mistress of it but, by her great charity and humility, she does not want people to concern themselves with her, but wishes to give everything to the Lord in secret; that the Lord God be the sole witness of her actions; for Him alone she likes to work in his vineyard. Her work is just, her aim upright; thus her actions are to be admired. The zeal she shows in action is something great, her faith has no limits: she submits everything to the judgment of others, though she is endowed with no little discernment; her energy in working is something… What reigns in that heart cannot be described.

She feels deeply and would not wish any human creature ever to suffer and would gladly take upon herself the labors of these who suffer, for whom she has such affection. And I can truly assure that she suffers far less from bearing the sufferings of others than from knowing or seeing those suffer for whom she has such affection.

Oh! creature of so generous a spirit, who possesses an inexpressible heart! How she has relieved me in the midst of horrible anguish! One feels capable of doing anything provided the oppressed is relieved. Her work, in which she is laboring with such zeal and which her heart pants to see completed: how pleasing to the Lord is this great anxiety of hers! And the work is as if she had already finished it; before God she stands so and for it she has doubled the merit. Blessed are you, who have known so well how to give back to the One who gave them to you the treasures, which will surely be doubled for you!

Friday

TC pp. 154-157, «Numerous young workers… ordination of my God»

At last, voices were heard from afar. Who can it be? A great number of young girls, who were running to meet me with all their strength! and I hastened my step more than ever. As soon as they saw me they exclaimed loudly:

- Blessed be you in the Lord! A terrible hurricane carried everything away from us and, however much we begged the Lord to come to our aid, seeing ourselves lost, we could obtain nothing. Only a young gentleman told us to go along this road, that we would find a farmer who would accept us to work in the vineyard of the Lord. And, from the description he gave us, it is you!

And all vying with one another pressed close to me.

- Well then, tell me what was this gentleman like?

- Very handsome!

- And where did he stay?

- We do not know!

I gathered them and invited them to follow me, because there was still a path marked out. And so they did. But after walking long, some began to tell me that they did not feel up to making so long a journey and so disastrous, and preferred to go back. There were no reasons to convince them. How much pain I suffered! But others still, in the end that half of them remained halfway. What my anxiety was I cannot describe.

At last we find a good shepherd and, greeting us, he invites us to his house. And what mercy! he makes us a gift of his estate, and asked me to have it worked for the greater glory of God. I did not delay in putting all these workers in their places and left one of them as guide. A strong voice, which imposed on me to do it as soon as possible and to go back to help those who would not come with me.

Weary, without delay I turn back; but hardly had I taken a few steps when a rough man comes close to me and says to me:

- Run, for those creatures you left on the way are dying. I stop, seized by the thought that the voice I had heard so strongly was He, that I am to go toward sufferings. They are the cause of their own harm and, surely, now they would want help. I was perplexed, when my angel comes near me:

- Jesus forgave the lost sheep and went seeking her to bring her back to the flock (cf. Lk 15:4-7). Charity must have neither reasons nor limits.

So, the voice was my angel's and, much mortified, I ran to find them again. Arrived at the first ones, they were battered from much ill treatment received from the infernal dragon. Finally arrived at the others, who very nearly had fallen into the infernal precipice, gathered all together, we prostrated ourselves on the ground to thank the Most High and to beg his grace and mercy.

In this land of labor, where nothing but thistles and crosses are found, only the grace of God is the comfort of immortal souls, for whom only the passage from this life to blessed eternity remains.

Continuing to converse, we came to a cottage. My voice:

- Stop! for here there are good people and you will find something to put these poor peasant women to work. I was surprised to see again those two good old people who had sheltered me another time, but far distant from these regions: they were other fields, a different cottage, but the two old people were the ones who welcomed me with great joy and handed over to me their estate, begging me to put my workers there.

The estate set in order, I only lacked the one to leave in charge of directing these inexperienced peasant women. The good old woman, seeing me so pensive, begged me to tell her why I was worried, and I told her:

- For having no one to entrust these workers to. She herself offered and assured me that she would take great pains, that I need not fear in continuing my journey, that, when I find her, I should send her to her. I thought it was the ordination of my God.

Saturday

TC pp. 358-360, «On the bed of suffering all… to weave flowers and laurel»

Setting myself to pray with great fervor, I thanked my God and waited eagerly for the hour when I could receive Him within this His breast, for I possessed nothing of my own. After I had stayed a good while with my God, my voice made me feel that it was no longer time to linger, but to go to someone who was very ill. I obeyed and, flying, went to help one who was groaning. I found poor creatures all numb with cold, who stirred compassion; besides, they were very grave, for lack of care. It was heartbreaking to see them. Having settled them as best I could, comforted and lifted in spirit, they seemed all reborn to a new life.

For those sick people, for whom there was no longer any remedy, all that remained was to seek first the comfort of the soul and then to save them and exhort them to resignation, encouraging them that they would soon enjoy the fruit of their resignation and of the sufferings my God sent them. How I tried to make them see this sweet and beautiful passage, like one setting out on a journey to see a delightful city!

And so I managed to lift those spirits frightened by the nearness of death. They talked with me about how they would carry out the errands I gave them: that they should ask my God for pity and mercy on my behalf, that they should greet my holy protectors.

- Oh! when you see the majestic sovereign Queen of heaven, pray for me!

They were so enthusiastic that they no longer thought of fearful death, but only of making acts of love and repentance so as to pass, by these, quickly from the antechamber of purgatory to the beautiful heavenly homeland.

A pastor came up to me and said:

- Oh! is this the graceful way to prepare these wretches, who deserve it so little?

- Oh! - with a lofty look I said to him - What? Are these not creatures of my God? Though rough and ignorant and sinners, they too have a soul, which must be united to its center. And is it perhaps only the rich who must be comforted? and only they have a humanity that deserves relief? and have they not sinned too, as unfortunately I also sinned, poor slave? Oh! how badly these words sound to me! On the bed of suffering, which is preparing us for the great journey, we are all equal: the great, the poor, we all need help and assistance. For these poor creatures it is harder than for the rich to find help and relief.

He fell silent, and looked at me in surprise because I was doing what I had been given to do so that (a poor sick man), joyful and contrite, might fly to eternal rest. And my two good creatures entrusted to him I kept with me; these wretches were too many. Having settled them, we tried to find a bed where they could lie down; none was found and these creatures were tired. I found one and judged it right to yield it to these creatures.

At last, worn out, I lay down where a woman had died shortly before. Oh! it served me well, for I so longed to lie down. I stayed on this filthy bed two hours. When I was in deep sleep, a lament woke me: it was a poor woman asking for help, afflicted with a terrible illness: leprosy!

Without looking at what it was, I ran to help her and embraced her, to ease her of the anguish of the illness; and I called the good chaplain, so that he might give her the last comforts of holy Church.

This good religious came and, seeing that I held her in my arms to ease her, cried out that I should draw away from so cruel a disease. But no! I told him not to fear. Meanwhile she expired, comforted by the Lord, because she bore Him with her in her breast.

But what the charitable priest said came true exactly: the disease showed itself in me and I fell ill. I was dying when an angel, or rather a soul of the Lord, came to heal me. I regained strength and my voice commanded me to depart and go to a field, where flowers and laurel had to be woven».

8th Sunday in Ordinary Time

FS pp. 201-202, «Trust in God’s providence… in it providence»

The Institute adopted, at the initiative of Fr. Tornatore, most devoted to the first Person of the Trinity, the practice of dedicating the month of January as the month of the eternal Father (cf. Letter to D. G. Granito di Belmonte: 8-1-1887, 16-1-1889).

No less tender and trusting was her devotion to the Holy Spirit, «joy of hearts», in which He has the mission of reviving divine love and consuming every earthly affection (M 1.1, p. 39). In 1872, when she found herself so alone, without the guidance of a director, she felt secure under that of her «governing Spirit»:

«What a consolation it is for me, who am so abandoned by all human help, to have my dear Spirit, who guides me in everything, directs me and sustains me so well, even in the days of such painful state. He works and leads everything with excellence. I find nothing but misery and shame and confusion» (M 3, pp. 9, 11f).

Trust in the divine fatherhood, which Jesus asks of his disciples, is not only, in Mother Rosa’s life, an effect of faith, but also a fact experienced almost daily, even in the form of real miracles, regarding the path of the Institute, especially in economic straits. She frequently notes the immediate effect of prayer in such situations: an unknown person who brings what is needed to pay a debt, unexpected provisions arriving from afar at the right moment, the solution of a difficulty when things seem most tangled… (cf. M 1.1, pp. 71f, 103, 145; 3, pp. 61f, 65f; 4.1, pp. 7, 85-87; 4.4, p. 99f; Letter to the Princess of Fitalia: 12-11-1889).

In general she does not turn to intermediary intercessors, but entrusts herself directly to the most holy Trinity, to the eternal Father. She feels reassured by the promise made to her by the Lord: «You will have all that you need» (M 1.1, p. 103, 118). It seems to her quite normal that, since it is the Work of God, He should come to meet the difficulties that will arise. In fact, from time to time the promise is renewed to her:

«I wept: I told my eternal Father to send me his providence: He appeared to me so beautiful that I was in ecstasy, and He told me very clearly that everything necessary for his Work He would take care of» (M 1.1, p. 172).

One day, amid external difficulties, she complained to the Lord: «Tell me, my Love, why do you not hear me?». And she had the immediate answer: «I have refused you nothing of what you asked me» (M 1.1, p. 143).

She would have wished her spiritual daughters, in particular the superiors of the houses, to be animated by the same trust to the point of wresting the miracle from God the Father, if necessary. She repeats it frequently in her letters. She writes to one of them:

«I feel the providence of God so strongly in me, and I would like to be able to pass it on to all the daughters of St. Anne» (to Sr. A. Aquilina Gilardoni: 22-7-1892).

She was fully convinced that, when we leave to God the care of ourselves and our affairs, thinking only of Him, He will take care of our problems, according to the recommendation of St. Peter (1 Pet 5:7):

«Providence will come, do not be anxious… God will take care of us, if we think only of Him. Have the novena for providence to St. Joseph repeated and ask him to give you humility, and through this virtue to give you providence in it» (Letter to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni: 3-8-1872).

Monday

FS pp. 196-198, «God alone suffices… in her letters to the superiors»

She very frequently expresses her aspiration, common to all souls accustomed to infused contemplation, to isolate herself from all that is not God and to remain alone with Him. She wrote on 17 January 1875:

«A voice said to me thus:

- Live only in God and seek nothing else. Converse with Him and seek no other relief but in Him. In Him let everything suffice you…

- Yes, my Good, only in you!» (M 4.3, p. 15).

There are moments - she says - when «the world, all creatures are secondary objects, as if apart, worthy of attention only to gather the fruits to offer to my Beloved Good» (M 4.3, p. 56).

In the book Labors and Consolations, answering a «pastor» who tried to disturb her about her walking without a guide, she inserts a beautiful outpouring in which she expresses all that God represents in her journey of faith:

«I beg you to speak only of the greatness of God and of his omnipotence and mercy. These three subjects alone give me great satisfaction, both in hearing them spoken of and in pausing to reason about them alone…

Oh! the mind reasons and in such immensity has room to run without ever meeting a stumbling block that halts its reasoning. The intellect unfolds to the greatest knowledge of the soul in its relations with its God, that endless ocean of greatness, power and mercy.

The more the mind enters into it, the greater it sees the space and ever new arguments unfold, and the majesty of a God is distinguished in wider proportions. And, as the soul is always subject to Him, how it groans painfully when, through the darkness in which it finds itself wrapped because of sin, it feels itself estranged from Him!» (TC, p. 313).

What in her was a maturing of faith, strengthened by unitive experience, she impressed upon the daughters of St. Anne as the goal of the necessary affective purification. On 17 October 1898 she gave the novices a warm exhortation on the true love of God, and said to them:

«A religious must always think of Jesus, love Him and be wholly His… What a beautiful thing to be completely detached from relatives, from superiors, from that sick person, from the confessor!…» (FIOCCHI, II, p. 281).

Whoever loves God cannot remain indifferent before the offense against so great a Good. We have already seen to what degree Mother Rosa’s heart suffered on seeing God offended.

«Only one thing frightens and alarms me: the offense of God», she repeats in her letters to the superiors.

Tuesday

FS pp. 55-56, «Her own sufferings… He taught me many things»

The certainty of forgiveness will not prevent her, however, from finding in the memory of the offenses done to God a reason to humble herself with expressions such as this: «My wickedness allows nothing, because I am infamous» (M 1.1, p. 39, year 1866).

Her own sufferings and her compassion for others who suffered had prepared her for the encounter with the Crucified, in whom every mystery of human pain finds explanation and comfort. Moreover, feeling redeemed and forgiven led her to an ever more passionate love for the wounded Savior. Thus she began to open to the gift of infused contemplation.

It was during the novena of Our Lady of the Vineyards that she felt favored with great consolations, with visions, interior words and a deep joy never before experienced. Afterward she also experienced dryness and abandonment, to the point of losing peace: «because I did not yet know - she reasons - how to fight under the banner of the holy Cross, delightful and dear; but how many are committed by being a beginner!».

Her director helped her recover interior stillness by making her understand the meaning of those alternations of fervor and aridity, of light and darkness on the way of perfection. And she goes on narrating and commenting:

«O dear Jesus! Yes, let us become fond of Calvary and in suffering we shall see its delights; drawing near to the object that is loved all suffering becomes a balm that is desired.

In the caresses He often gave me, He presented me with something of his gifts, such as that of meditation, and this after holy Communion, pressed to my Good, which was more a contemplation than meditation, because He placed me in a wound and there I stayed for hours and was not aware of being alive, and it always grew more in me. At other times I was absorbed and, as in conversation, I remained with my Jesus. He taught me many things» (M 1.1, pp. 3-5).

Wednesday

TC p. 347, «Very calm I reached a hovel… there is much to do!»

Very calm I reached a hovel, much ill-treated, because I had suffered greatly and felt I was about to faint. And so it happened. I abandoned myself and spent the whole night between spasms and lifelessness. I commended myself much to my Crucified that He might give me strength. There was a moment when I felt my soul detach itself, and I thought I was taking refuge in the side of my Savior, weeping:

- My God! do not leave me: I feel I am dying!

For a good while I understood nothing; I was only in a sweetness of paradise. Shaken, I said: Where am I? My Crucified:

- You are with me! You suffered much and this was necessary. Restore yourself and work, for there is much to do!

Thursday

TC p. 156, «Weary without delay… to put these poor peasant women to work»

Weary, without delay I turn back; but hardly had I taken a few steps when a rough man came up to me and said:

- Run, for those creatures you left on the road are dying. I stop, seized by the thought that the voice I had heard so strongly was He, that I must go to the pains. They are the cause of her suffering and, surely, now they would want help. I was perplexed when my angel came up to me:

- Jesus forgave the lost little sheep and went to look for her to bring her back to the flock (cf. Lk 15:4-7). Charity must have neither reasons nor limits.

So, the voice was my angel’s and, very mortified, I ran to find them again. Arriving at the first ones, they were ill-treated by the many mistreatments received from the infernal dragon. Finally arriving at the others, who had almost fallen into the infernal precipice, gathered all together, we prostrated ourselves on the ground to thank the Most High and beg his grace and mercy.

In this land of toil, where nothing but thorns and crosses is found, only the grace of God is the comfort of immortal souls, for whom only the passage from this life to blessed eternity remains.

As I went on reflecting, we reached a hovel. My voice:

- Stop! for here there are good people and you will find something to put these poor peasant women to work.

Friday

TC pp. 100-101, «A soul comes up to me… I would never have wanted it to end»

A soul so beautiful and sweet comes up to me; it assures me that those people roar, but they will be able to do nothing to me.

- Tell me, please, blessed soul, who sent you? Perhaps you are a heavenly messenger, and my God sent you here to defend his field? Tell me what you kept in your heart.

At these words, spoken with great haste to get the answers, (it added):

- I have nothing more to tell you. And I remained sad.

- Why this sadness of yours? You have quite other things to tell me!

It comes close to me and, in an act of compassion, reasons about the future of my cultivation: what infinite fields would grow in it; and something beautiful that my God took pleasure in and with his visits made them fruitful, leaving them great treasures.

- Oh! how happy I would be to be able to find Him! For pity’s sake, tell me in which field He usually goes, for I want to find Him.

With an angelic smile it answered me that He is in the same field where I am, that it is not the workers who do much of that work, but the Lord himself who brings the work to completion, giving it an exquisite beauty.

But I still did not feel satisfied with its words, and I would have wanted it to tell me other sublime things about my Good. But it fell asleep and, however much I begged it to wake, I could never obtain it. The thought came to me that it might not be sleep, but rapture; I fell silent and placed myself near it as if I might hear something. Prostrate on the ground I begged my God to let me (hear) for a single instant. O goodness! drawing near, I heard the reasoning; it was so beautiful! it described the future of two souls, and of one who was at the point of death: how beautiful it was! I did not realize that gradually I was becoming absorbed. An interweaving of sufferings of a new kind: the end was an Eden of delights! When it ended, we reasoned together and I would never have wanted it to end.

Saturday

TC pp. 51-52, «Alone on the path of beloved suffering… I loved Him and love Him immensely!»

My Crucified! Halfway along, a serpent entrenched itself on my path: I stopped! Hissing loudly at me, with persuasive ways it invited me to turn back.
