I was bloodied, my limbs were all wounded: and I had made only half the way. Almost overcome by its words I was about to turn back, but my Crucified stopped me and gave me balm for my wounds. The most bitter pain calmed, He put the dragon to flight; but far too much remained to climb!

My Crucified! He left me alone and, like the bride of the Songs (cf. Song 3:1-3), I went wandering through that forest seeking Him, taking a step forward on the path and another back. All the little branches were dry and all interwoven in the sign of a cross.

- You too, do you join my sadness? - I kept saying; and I stopped.

My Crucified with a great cross on his shoulders! He placed it on mine and, taking from me the terror of suffering, left me an ardent love for it. I loved Him much and love Him immensely!

9th Sunday in Ordinary Time

FS pp. 64, «Confused before such condescension… He taught great things»

Confused before such condescension of God, annihilated in her own smallness and misery, on 28 May 1864 she poured out her heart in these terms:

«What are you doing, my Beloved? Have you forgotten my wickedness? You fill me with your treasures, and what more can I give you? All that I had I already gave you and, because I am a poor creature, having given what I had - life, will, everything! - nothing is left to me. Oh! how small a thing the creature is before your infinite greatness! a nothing and less than nothing. Yes… the soul, which is a portion of you, my Good, longs to re-enter its center, which is my Being…

Reasoning thus, I became absorbed and found myself in Him in the greatest ecstasy. I saw very great and infinite things. My Beloved seemed to pour into me something I cannot express. He taught me great things…» (M 1.2, p. 2f).

Monday

TC pp. 81-82, «Comforted by a… to walk on that long path»

Alone again!

I did not know whether I should get up and set out again or wait for morning. I hear a person approaching with slow steps: Alas! my God, I am lost! More than ever wrapping myself in that thicket, I waited for him to pass. I hear him stop and, with a long sigh, offer a prayer to the most holy Virgin in thanksgiving. Poor me! He went on praying and addressed most beautiful prayers to the Virgin. My God! thorns had entered from every part of my body and I felt myself fainting from pain.

Meanwhile day broke. And oh! what a surprise! It was a son of St. Francis of Assisi who, as soon as he saw me, said:

- Are you here?

All trembling I answered him:

- For pity’s sake, tell me where I am! I am alone, abandoned by my God. I can no longer find where. I walked a long time and found myself in the same field. Tell me something of what my God told you. Is it He who sent you here?

- Oh! is it not He - the friar resumed - who saved you from the destruction that those evildoers wrought in the field?

And he told me the event. I was frantic to know whether my God was He who took pleasure in so much of my suffering.

- Tell me - I said to him - what He told you.

I saw him rapt in ecstasy and, at that sight, I fell face down on the ground, weeping, immersed in my nothingness and annihilated, torn by pain, because I was unworthy of being able to see and converse with my Good too. I took such an aversion to myself that I would have dissolved from the pain I felt, and I was about to faint when the servant of my God told me that I was greatly loved by God and that He took great pleasure in my suffering; and he told me many things, exhorting me to walk on that long path.

Tuesday

TC pp. 210-211, «When the good is not according to the will… is off the path»

- When the good is not according to the will of God, it is not perfect. What man has created of his own head, to satisfy an ambition and become an object of admiration, has no lasting, his building will soon be torn down.

He listened to me with a certain sneer; he little liked my words. He said.

«If you do not believe that it is the work of the Lord, why do you not try to introduce them on your path?»

«You say it with your lips, but!…

Hearing this, he becomes furious, shouts and begins to call me names; he threatens to accuse me of having blasphemed because I did not speak according to the doctrine of the Church.

«Do so! my judge is my Master!»

«Then, who are you?»

«See, O good pastor, that you are mistaken, because I am a poor slave who can do nothing else but what my Master has commanded me.

He looks around, and then resumes:

«Tell me, where is this Master of yours? After a long sigh:

«Oh! do you not know Him?»

At this answer he calls me a fool; and I see that my time is wasted. He turns away and leaves me.

Oh! my Love! this man wants to work and does not know for whom he works or where?

Folly of the ambitious man! he wants to be, to do, and concludes nothing, because he is off the path.

Wednesday

FS p. 100, «Another premise to keep in mind… we shall deal with later»

Another premise to keep in mind: Mother Rosa lists endlessly interior lights, penetrations of hearts, foreknowledge of future events, visions…, but she never speaks of revelations, never of messages to bring to anyone, and we never see her regulate her own way of acting and her own decisions according to what she has seen or understood, although at times she feels bound to forewarn, in the strictest secrecy, her confidants. She feels guided by God, taught and upheld by her Good, which gives her such trust and assurance, with regard to the Lord’s Work, that she faces every unpleasant situation with serenity, precisely because she is convinced that she is a pure and useless instrument of the divine plan. But we shall deal further on with this awareness of her mission as foundress.

Thursday

FS pp. 195-196, «The virginal heart… to know God the supreme Good»

The virginal heart, while succeeding in freeing the affective potential to polarize it in uncreated Love, increases the capacity to love all that God loves. Such polarization becomes all the more fruitful and effective the more vital the union with the supreme Good.

One of the first manifestations of true love, guided by faith, is piety, the true kind, not devotional or sentimental piety, which interposes itself between the soul and God and takes from love that dynamic restlessness of one who lives not for self but for God and for others. Rosa Gattorno knew how to direct, at the crucial moment of her life, the richness of her affectivity so as to develop an authentic piety centered on the fundamental contents of faith: the Trinity-God, Jesus Christ, the Virgin Mary, some model saints and protectors, the Church, the Institute, her spiritual daughters, the poor.

She wrote on the first page of her Memoirs, concerning the decision made in 1858 to give herself fully to God: «By the grace of the Lord I noticed that all earthly affections were dissipating; nothing was tasty to me any more: only my God was the pasture of all my delights» (M 1.1, p. 1).

In the fervent, very frequent conversations with God, she loves to address Him with titles of deep meaning: the Being of my living, my All, my Good, the supreme Good, Love… She also loves to contrast her own smallness with the «infinite sea of the greatness of God», that ineffable divine essence in comparison with which «whoever comes to taste it finds all that is earthly makes him nauseous» (M 1.2, p. 2). She, who has the experiential light of such greatness, cannot understand «how man can live without knowing God, the supreme Good» (M 11.2, p. 78f).

Friday

D. pp. 122-123, par. 3

The Voice Asks for Adherence to God’s Plan.

It trains her to walk in step with God, who shows in his interventions that his will is inexhaustible, that the ultimate end toward which He leads her is known only to Him, that she cannot content herself with having the certainty of the norms approved by human authority. But she must open herself every day to the newness of the Spirit.

Early on she understands through the Voice that God’s will sends her where she could not have imagined. She listens like Abraham: «Go from your country, your kindred and your father’s house to the land that I will show you» (Gen 12:1), and follows the path indicated by God.

At the moment of the decision to found the Institute in Piacenza, battling the doubt that what she was living might be an illusion and might not correspond to God’s will, in prayer she hears:

«A clear Voice: «All my will what happened, peace, peace, everything will be smoothed out»» (M. 2, p. 47).

Rosa silently loves and adores her God who is revealing himself through the Voice. She finds herself living, perhaps without being aware of it, the experience of Moses who hangs upon the Voice (Ex 3:4) of «He Who Is» to face the risks of the mission, the responsibility (Ex 5:22-23) of guiding and governing a people with a law (Ex 19:20) toward holiness, the concern to give water and nourishment to those who thirst and hunger (Ex 16:17), the unforeseen events of the long and wearisome pilgrimage (Ex 33:7-17; 34ff). As to Isaiah: «A Voice says: «Cry out»… lift up your voice, do not fear» (Is 40:6-9), and to other prophets the Voice demands to announce the future, to affirm God’s will and denounce errors, to her too it makes known in advance events or calamities so that she may take part in them with her prayer. Through the Voice the Lord communicates to her his love for man:

«A Voice answered me: «Yes, I love man immensely»…».

«…You, if one may say so, are mad for man and he? A Voice that tells me: «Yes, I love him much» (M. 1.1, p. 152; M. 1.2, p. 1).

Saturday

D. pp. 66-68, par. 3

The Mystery of the Poverty of Jesus.

Called to identify with the divine Victim, Christ in the mystery of his poverty, she contemplates various aspects of this reality of his. She sees him small, in the likeness of the Child Jesus, he trains her to value every smallest gesture, to clothe herself in his smallness:

«All at once behold my little Jesus, together with a little angel also in the act of adoring him. Now that I write I no longer even know how to move the pen. Behold, he wanted me also to write for whom I have been offering my fasts for years! I am smaller than an insect and so I do small things, and even these trifles are accepted by my Good. Monday is for the souls in purgatory, Tuesday for sinners and the dying, Wednesday for St. Francis of Assisi and St. Joseph, Thursday I offer it to the Eternal Father in honor of Jesus in the Sacrament, Friday for my children that he may keep them good Christians for me, Saturday in honor of Most Holy Mary, Sunday for the Holy Church and the Supreme Pontiff, Cardinals, Bishops. Why, Jesus, do you like me to write this too? So I said to him, but I received nothing, only a great consolation I feel for having written it and a fire that consumes me (M. 1.1, p. 161).

Jesus is an unsurpassable and jealous guide in the most demanding moments of the Foundation:

«I turned to my Good and begged him to tell me how I should conduct myself and I was instructed how I should do and say… My Good had equipped me with his strength…» (M. 1.1, p. 56).

10th Sunday in Ordinary Time

FS pp. 154-156, «Suffering as Mother Rosa sees it… too beautiful you are to me»

Suffering, as Mother Rosa sees it, is the normal condition of following Christ in this earthly exile; if God, now and then, opens to us a flash of light and consolation, it is only to help our weakness. Her personal existence was almost a pilgrimage in the dark through the desert, only brightened by some refreshing oasis. Only one who follows Jesus to Golgotha and to the agony of the cross shares in the triumph of his glory.

«On Tabor one can stay only to take a little refreshment, and Jesus is accustomed to bring there the weak souls who, if he does not refresh them, die on the way; but the strong (go) always forward, by dint of spurring, until they reach Golgotha and there crucified with Him, to rise all beautiful, luminous, and enter triumphant into glory in heaven» (Letter to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 12-8-1870).

This very hope of eternal glory must sustain loving souls in the sufferings of this life; here is the time to suffer, there will be the time to rejoice.

«A brief suffering for an eternal rejoicing», she often repeats. And she likes to quote the well-known couplet of St. Francis of Assisi: So great is the good I await - that every pain is a delight to me (cf. Letter to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 3-10-1867; to Sr. A. Aquilina Gilardoni: 5-1-1886).

But already in this exile suffering itself becomes ineffable enjoyment for one who knows how to discover the treasures hidden in it:

«One feels the suffering and does not suffer, because every pain is bound up with an abyss of unequaled joy»

- «Whoever has never tasted the delights of suffering does not know what it means to rejoice»

- «Who can describe the taste of suffering? No one. At least so I think, because not even I, the more I study it the less I know how to explain it. What a mystery: to rejoice so much in such horrible pains!»

- «My Good, my only treasure, what are my pains before so much consolation?… Press your arm down even more, make me suffer more, if for so little you give me so much!» (M 1.1, pp. 119, 179; 1.2, p. 69; 4.1, p. 107).

And here appears the alternative, by now classic, that St. Teresa of Avila formulated in these terms: Either to suffer or to die! and which St. Mary Magdalene de’ Pazzi modified in this form: To suffer and not to die! The dilemma revives each time the sweet thought of death surfaces in Mother Rosa’s mind as the end of suffering (cf. M 1.1, pp. 137-139). She writes in the month of March 1878: «Today I had another piece of news about my death. Oh! sweet life, dying! But to suffer and not to die would be my choice. Only because I will no longer be able to suffer does it grieve me, but too beautiful you are to me!» (M 4.5, p. 44; cf. Letter to Sr. A. Aquilina Gilardoni: 5-1-1886).

Monday

FS pp. 180-181, «Contradictions, misunderstandings… ministers of the Church»

Contradictions, misunderstandings, persecutions are the normal heritage of all who commit themselves to following Christ. The life of Rosa Gattorno could not be an exception. Ever since she accepted, by God’s will, her mission as foundress she understood that it is the mark of every evangelical enterprise to have to face, first of all, the postulates of human prudence and then the opposition, not only of the enemies of the interests of the Kingdom, but also of the good and well-intentioned who do not share or do not understand the viewpoints of one who acts under divine impulse.

She had the awareness of being an instrument of God, though unskilled: her foundation was the Work of God. It is no wonder that in every opponent she saw an adversary of God’s plan, indeed an unconscious collaborator of the evil one. Hence her deep suffering, especially when she discovered in the opponents hypocrisy, ulterior motives and hidden personal interests. Let us not forget, moreover, her tendency to turn every unforeseen event into a reason and opportunity to suffer. In reality she had to bear true slanders, all the more painful as they came from persons to whom she had given trust, affection and sacrifice (cf. FIOCCHI, I, pp. 181f, 186-189, 199-220); or from those whom she deeply revered as ministers of the Church.

Tuesday

FS pp. 258-260, «She would like to make of each daughter of St. Anne… missionaries»

She would like to make of each daughter of St. Anne a spokeswoman of Jesus to let all men hear the message of the Love that saves; that all might have the gift she experiences when she feels she is a pure instrument of Him who makes her speak.

She wrote to her close friend Sr. A. Celsa Speranza:

«Jesus will put on your tongue words that not even you will know how you pronounced them… Love, and think that it was Jesus who spoke in your heart and you were his echo, another» (Undated letter, n. 76).

What matters is, first of all, to evangelize with life (Circ. Letter 20-8-1895). One of the sisters testifies at the informative process: «She wanted and required us to act as missionaries in the hospitals, first by our bearing and then by charity and, finally, by word» (Summ., p. 650).

Mother Rosa’s apostolic heart had two moments of deep joy: one, when she gave her maternal embrace to the sixteen sisters of the first expedition that left for Latin America on 23 November 1878, a sign of rapid expansion on that continent; and the other, the day she presented to Leo XIII the four members of the first mission to East Africa, November 1886.

In her many letters to the missionary sisters one feels her heart throb as with a holy envy of the fortune they enjoy of being able to labor and suffer in the vanguard of the Kingdom of God. She would have liked to have so many daughters of St. Anne as to satisfy all the requests that reached her. She wrote to the superior in Eritrea, Sr. A. Pierina Della Valle:

«My God, what a pain not to have sisters!… Come, up! courage! I wish I were ten years younger and had strength; I would go and be a cobbler! But I am very old and always very poorly» (Letter of 8-11-1895).

From St. Francis of Assisi she had learned to see in the missionary vocation a free response to divine inspiration; the superiors of the houses in Italy had to keep her informed of the sisters who showed «vocation to go to the missions», but had to add «an exact and scrupulous report on their conduct», in order to guarantee the good choice of the missionaries (Circ. Letter 25-3-1887, 23-4-1893).

Wednesday

FS p. 287, «Although her first… the way of paradise it is written: Obedience»

Although her first concern was to form the superiors in the art of governing well, since usually when one governs well one obeys well, she did not fail to inculcate in all the daughters of St. Anne the life of obedience, which «is the pivot of true holiness» (Circ. Letter: 1-1-1889).

«Obey if you wish to be holy», she repeated in the communities (Letter to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 4-5-1869).

«On the way of paradise it is written: Obedience» (M 4.4, p. 14).

Thursday

Tr. pp. 79-80, «In him and through him… you all his holy ones»

In him and through him everything is explained and everything finds its reason and its single meeting point. One then understands well the meaning of the words in the great prayer of Jesus: «Holy Father, keep in unity those whom you have given me, that they may be one, as you Father in me and I in you… that the world may believe that you have sent me. And the glory you have given me I have given them, that they may be one as we are one» (Jn 17:20-21). Here is the way of Christian perfection and holiness: to become one with Jesus, to identify progressively with Him, to become one with the Father and the Holy Spirit. The way to attain such unity was lived and taught by Mother Rosa, eager to become one with Christ crucified.

To put hope into practice is then to insert it into love for the Crucified. From this derives the lively and perennial relevance of Mother Rosa’s charism, who could well say with St. Paul: «I decided to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ and him crucified» (1 Cor 2:2).

This was also Mother Rosa’s wisdom (especially mystical). But this wisdom is nothing other than ardent love for Jesus and particularly for Jesus crucified, as can easily be deduced from the data of her life and her mystical writings. The love of God, in fact, is a source of light and wisdom, as the Aquinate openly affirms: «The ardor of charity is changed into the light of knowledge and wisdom» (Commentary on the Gospel of St. John, c. V).

Mother Rosa’s life was so united with that of Jesus, particularly with Jesus crucified, that she could say with St. Paul: «I have been crucified with Christ and it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me» (Gal 2:20); and again: «for me to live is Christ» (Phil 1:21). Mother Rosa’s mystical experience reached these marvelous heights. At the base of so many mystical graces, with which she was gifted by God, was this painful, joyful and luminous identification with Jesus crucified. All the wealth of Mother Rosa’s mystical graces (and they are many) flowers from this fundamental reality: love for Christ crucified, whom she calls «my Good».

In the person of Jesus, therefore, the history of the old and new Covenant finds its origin and foundation. Their unity is constituted by Jesus who is to come, Jesus who has come, Jesus who comes. The old Covenant was a prelude and prophecy of what would be revealed and accomplished in the new Covenant personified in Jesus Christ, Son of the Father and Son of Mary, through his examples (Jesus teaches more by deeds than by words) and above all by the full adherence of His will to that of the Father at the supreme moment of accepting passion and death. The old Covenant is then changed into a song of love for God and neighbor, love practiced and preached by Jesus Christ and already anticipated in many Psalms: «I love you, Lord, my strength» (Ps 18:2); «Love the Lord, all you his holy ones» (Ps 31:24).

Friday

FS pp. 150-152, «Carrying the cross with Jesus… of his most beloved brides»

The suffering of the Christian, according to the invitation of Jesus (Mt 10:38; Lk 9:23; 14:27) and the theology of St. Paul (Gal 2:19; 6:14), has a name: the Cross. And it is the name preferred by Mother Rosa. She confesses that even in 1859, enticed by the great consolations of those beginnings, she was not accustomed to «fight under the banner of the holy Cross, delightful and dear». She was a «beginner» (M 1.1, p. 4). But she was not long in entering fully into the school of the Cross: this will always be her «companion», her «bed of rest» (M 3, p. 25). One day when she was full of bitterness, holding the cross very tight, she spoke thus with it: «Is it true, my treasure, that you are always my companion?». And she heard a voice that comforted her: «Only from the Cross does one learn to love!» (TC, p. 329).

Not content with constantly having the image of the Crucified before the eyes of body and spirit, she wished to make her love tangible by tying a small cross tightly to her breast, taking her brief rest lying on a cross and often remaining hanging on a large wooden cross she had in her little room in Piacenza. But it was the very mystery of the Cross, more than its materiality, that had shaped her life.

And she would have wished each of the daughters of St. Anne to become a true lover of the Cross. Encouragements in this sense are very frequent in her letters; here are some:

«Courage on the way of Calvary, if you wish to be crucified with your Beloved and die with Him on the delightful bed of the Cross»

- «Every day new, a new cross! Blessed is the one whose dawn breaks amid thorns and pains!»

- «In paradise there is no more cross, there are no more sufferings there: only Love, Love… Cheerful, cheerful, for Jesus likes those who suffer: whoever does not want to suffer does not want to love!»

- «Whoever wishes to follow me - says the Master showing us a cross, - let him take up his cross and follow me. So, what language is this, heavenly Spouse? O blessed souls! He gives me that treasure which the world does not know and which He offers to his beloved brides, and indeed He seeks that it be heavy, so that one may come one day to taste his delights»

- «This holy Wood, nuptial bed of his most beloved brides!» (Letter to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 27-5-1869, 1-1-1870; to Sr. Adelaide Pezzoni: 1869, 16-1-1870; to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino: 23-12-1868, 6-2-1870).

Saturday

FS p. 213, «Every day she made… upon them the choicest blessings»

Every day she made as it were an offering to the eternal Father, in the mercy seat of the Heart of Jesus, of her Institute, not as an organized and working structure, but as a living reality, made up of individual persons, each with her vocation, her effort of sanctification, her responsibilities, her problems. It was her prayer as foundress:

«My God! to you I entrust these creatures you have entrusted to me. Now I place them for all this time in the Heart of your Son Jesus, and may you cover them with heavenly dew, that they may be defended from the slightest encounter. In this loving retreat of the Heart of Jesus may they learn the true school of your divine Love. My God, bless them and strengthen them in suffering, pour upon them the choicest blessings» (Letter to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti: 25-5-1871).

11th Sunday in Ordinary Time

FS p. 71, «The habit of contemplation… as if another were saying them»

The habit of unitive contemplation becomes ever more natural, effortlessly she manages to keep her mind constantly fixed on God, she feels enveloped by God’s presence, accompanied by Him even in the affairs to be dispatched, in work and in travel; but in the solitude of night is where she abandons herself to union:

«I do not hold a thought that is earthly. I work, I act because my Good is always with me. It has already been four days and nights that He is always visible at my side; every now and then I cannot help, while working, (saying to Him): Alas! you make me die! Ah! pity me, my Beloved, step away, for I am dying! But at night I do not say so: wholly in Him I abandon myself and my sleep is a continual ecstasy. Oh! if God is with me, who can be against me? (cf. Rom 8:31). The whole world is a nothing, less than nothing; for me all that I see on earth is rottenness» (M 1.1, p. 112).

It is an active presence, to the point of seeing herself almost replaced by the Lord, in the most delicate moments, He answering for her:

«I always find myself in the presence of God… There are times when I really feel certain words coming out of my mouth to answer in the affairs of his Work, and so I never think what I must say, because my Love speaks for me and, at times, I can say that I listen to the very words with pleasure as if another were saying them…» (M 1.1, p. 149f).

Monday

FS pp. 181-182, «The account she herself gave… of what appears»

The account she herself gave of what happened in Piacenza on 31 March 1869 because of the slanderous accusations raised by the very superior of the house, is the best testimony of her behavior in similar cases and, above all, of her ready and generous forgiveness (M 1.2, pp. 21-28).

After summarizing the five persecutions suffered in the years 1868 and 1869, «fireworks on all sides», she adds: «Only one thing comforts me, and it is that no rancor has ever remained in me toward those who caused me so many pains and whoever they were, indeed I feel a very great affection toward them and for them I have increased my prayers, and I always tried to do them whatever good I could» (M 1.2, pp. 28-31).

And here too one of her most sincere introspections surprises us. One day the suspicion came to her that her above-mentioned tendency led her to discover malice where there was none and to magnify the causes of suffering out of a certain secret enjoyment in suffering; Jesus gave her the answer:

«My beloved, all that is done to you, I receive the same pain: your pains are mine. You want to know why you suffer so much pain at seeing your daughters and those you keep near you act so maliciously? Be calm, for there is nothing human in it; but since all that offends me you must feel painfully, so you feel more than appears» (M 1.1, p. 169f).

Tuesday

FS p. 195, «The virginal heart… the spiritual daughters, the poor»

The virginal heart, while succeeding in freeing the affective potential to polarize it in uncreated Love, increases the capacity to love all that God loves. Such polarization becomes all the more fruitful and effective the more vital the union with the supreme Good.

One of the first manifestations of true love, guided by faith, is piety, the true kind, not devotional or sentimental piety, which interposes itself between the soul and God and takes from love that dynamic restlessness of one who lives not for self but for God and for others. Rosa Gattorno knew how to direct, at the crucial moment of her life, the richness of her affectivity so as to develop an authentic piety centered on the fundamental contents of faith: the Trinity-God, Jesus Christ, the Virgin Mary, some model saints and protectors, the Church, the Institute, her spiritual daughters, the poor.

Wednesday

FS pp. 203-204, «God’s will, God’s taste… the object of our living»

God’s will, God’s taste, God’s good pleasure, God’s approval, are synonyms that also stand at the center of her pedagogy with the sisters:

«If you knew what consolation I feel merely in pronouncing this word - God’s taste - and even more, if the sweet thought of being or of being able to come to his good pleasure awakens vividly in me! I feel wholly beside myself, so that if I had to face the most cruel martyrdom, I would feel nothing…» (Letter to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni: 4-2-1871).

- «A thy will be done, said with resignation in time of battles and afflictions, is worth more than having the gift of raising the dead to life» (Letter to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 20-10-1871).

In the bitter months of 1872, when she had to suffer so much because of the affair of the Rules, her letters reflect the serenity of her spirit abandoned to God’s will.

«Let the whole world say: we do the will of God!» she writes to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa (11-6-1873).

So too in other moments of trials and sufferings. And when it becomes difficult to discover God’s will or one must await uncertain future events, there is the disposition of abandonment into God’s hands, never losing peace:

«Let us put everything into the most holy hands of God; may He do with us as He pleases» - «Cheerful, without worries, and trust in the Lord» - «Now I have done all my parts, God will do the rest» - «Let us leave it to the Lord, who works everything for the good of our soul» (Letter to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni: 1-7-1872; to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 25-1-1869, 6-8-1870, 9-3-1870).

«Let us leave everything in God’s hands…; may the divine will be fully accomplished in us: in it everything is satisfied, being for us the only object of our living» (Letter to Fr. Donadio: 22-4-1870).

Thursday

TC pp. 474-475, «You still have too much to work… I will give you in this heart of yours»

Overcome by weariness, I began to complain and said: But how long this road is! I am tired, I am cold and hungry, nothing can be found here, the eye cannot see either a haystack or a tree: all dry rocks! Surely night will come and, if this road is still always like this, I shall die of grief. So for me there is no longer any hope of getting out of here; everything before me is frightening.

And I walked on. The road kept getting worse and everything before me. The sun sets, hunger makes itself strongly felt, my strength is already failing: a great panic seizes me at having to succumb in the midst of that great stony ground. I look this way and that to see if I can find a blade of grass, because gladly would I have eaten it, but nothing! Throat dry, palate parched and not even a stream in sight to have a sip of water. I feel myself fainting and kneel with hands joined. I called my Master, my Lord and, crying out, told Him I was dying:

- Ah! come, help me: I am lost!

And I fainted. A soft voice says to me:

- Rise!

- Oh my Love! I am dying, you know?

He, with a smile:

- No! you have, my beloved, too much to work! Do not fear: my strength needs nothing. Run: before night you will find help. And He leaves me. Must I go away from here? Oh no! Here is my Good. And I kept looking fixedly at that place where I saw and heard Him. But my voice:

- Hasten to obey!

I seemed a giant of strength; I do not know whether I flew or truly walked. At dusk, I see in the distance a bell tower and hear its pealing. Oh my Love! it is your dwelling: a temple! tomorrow I shall feed on you. Oh! what a tight embrace I shall give you in this heart of yours!

Friday

TC pp. 397-398, «Now let us take a look at the fine work… Trust, and nothing else, says

my voice to me»

- Now let us take a look at the fine work my Master did. He not only dispelled everything, but used the evil to obtain a fertilizer for his fields, and we see them beautiful and vigorous. The trees put forth their foliage, the vines their delightful leaves, the pines and oaks are full of lovely bird nests that with their song weave lovely melodies. Whoever has the fortune to rest in the shade of these delightful plants enjoys peace and consolation.

She looks at me and, smiling, thanks me, and tries to work well and willingly. I set her to work and see that it is the lightest and least disastrous. So together we worked, when night overtook us without our noticing. She, almost frightened, said to me:

- What are we doing here in the middle of this field? We only talk of work and never seek to sustain ourselves. I answered her:

- Do not doubt, for my Master is that God who feeds the birds, and who can fear not having what he needs? (cf. Mt 6:26).

I look around and see nothing. The field was without trees, not even a farmhouse was in sight. My God! what will happen to this poor creature if she is not provided with what is necessary? Teach me what I must do.

- Trust, and nothing else - my voice tells me.

Saturday

TC pp. 476-477, «An important lady welcomes her… I try to love and serve God»

A good old woman stops and comes close to me:

- Come with me, it is not fitting that you stay here. Meanwhile he kept grumbling and calling me a vagabond: it was the least of the titles. This poor woman looked at me, and then said to the grumbler:

- Why do you abuse her so badly? Do you know that she is such as you believe?

- Surely! - he answered.

And she, the woman, in a resentful tone:

- I tell you that you are mistaken. Correct your terms. I am amazed and I will tell my mistress, who will surely take her defense.

And a charming squabble ensued. I stayed silent; she went on to say:

- You must know that my mistress was warned by a person that this creature was to arrive in the village and that she should be given lodging and refreshment.

Within me I felt a shiver, thinking of the words of my Lord: that I would find help. I looked at the woman, who took me by the hand, looked me over carefully and said:

- It is she: the description is exact.

She wanted to give me her arm, telling me she saw me so suffering that she feared I might have to suffer. I thanked her. A few steps on she entered a magnificent palace; the gracious lady came to meet me and said very loudly to that woman that she wanted me to be refreshed at once. And she begged me to tell her where I came from, how it was that she saw me so suffering; and she would have liked to know how I came to be so.

I anxiously would have liked to know who had told this woman that I was in such a state and put such charity in her heart; but I did not dare. She, meanwhile, did not stop asking me questions; I tried to reveal nothing and answered little. But she was not satisfied. She began to say in a more serious tone:

- But who are you?

I answered her:

- I am a poor slave of the Lord, by his obedience I find myself here. And with hands joined I turned to her asking who had told her that I was in such need. She looked at me, and then added:

- A noble gentleman, with a graceful horse, passed before me, who was in my garden, and told me to send my maid to the church door, that there was a creature who had great need of help and that whatever I did for her God would richly reward me. And I had to carry it all out, because I was left with such an impulse to fulfil what he told me. So I feel I love you and for you I feel an affection that I know I have never felt for any creature. I am alone, I live in seclusion in this castle and I try to love and serve God.

12th Sunday in Ordinary Time

FS pp. 254-255, «In 1867, while in Rome… I direct it to Him..»

In 1867, while in Rome, she went to the hospital. She wanted to satisfy that eagerness of hers to suck the sores of the sick, but had to desist, both so as not to attract attention and so as not to be rapt in ecstasy by spiritual sweetness (M 1.1, p. 61).

She taught the same spirituality to the daughters of St. Anne, that is, how to motivate charity by seeing Christ in the needy and the suffering. In the same year she wrote to the sisters of the hospital of Cento:

«Take comfort, you who labor for your Jesus. Ah! you are always conversing with Jesus, because in touching those sick people with charity, you touch Jesus… In those infirm creatures Jesus is found. Ah! what a thought, my daughters! I assure you that I feel I am dying of longing to come and be with you, to share in your charities…»

- «Seeing Jesus in the sick, how easy the meditation on the Passion of Jesus will be for you!» (Letter to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 23-4-1867; 7-1867).

It is interesting, however, to note an evolution with the passing of years, almost a purification of the motives of apostolic charity, the effect of a higher identification with the supreme Good. On 18 January 1875 Mother Rosa made the following profound introspection:

«Creatures, little by little, become for me an object to cultivate and love, no longer as I still know I felt a sensible compassion for their ills, or wished them all holy, yes, but looking at them as if in the help and good I did them, or at least thought I did, I found in them a certain pleasure, which the charity done seemed to me bound to bring them.

Now I find nothing, nothing: purely my Good. Not even the smallest of created things can I look at with a simple glance, if I do not first direct this too to Him…» (M 4.3, p. 18f).

Monday

Tr. pp. 139-140, par 1.2

Christ Jesus, the Holy One by essence, is He who makes «all the saints»

The Church ponders again the admonition of the apostle, who, urging the faithful to charity, exhorts them to have in themselves the same sentiments that were in Christ Jesus, who emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, becoming obedient unto death (cf. Phil 2:7-8), and for us, though he was rich, became poor (cf. 2 Cor 8:9).

Although the disciples must always manifest the imitation and witness of this charity and humility of Christ, mother Church rejoices to find in her bosom many men and women who follow more closely this self-emptying of the Savior and show it more clearly by embracing poverty and renouncing their own will; they, for love of God, in what concerns perfection, submit to man beyond the strict measure of the precept, in order to conform more fully to the obedient Christ. All the faithful, therefore, are invited and bound to pursue the holiness and perfection of their own state. Therefore let all strive to direct their affections rightly, so that the use of the things of this world and attachment to riches, contrary to the spirit of evangelical poverty, may not hinder them from tending to perfect charity, as the apostle indeed warns: «Those who use this world must not settle in it, for the form of this world is passing away» (cf. LG 42).

These texts, chosen among the many inspired ones, constitute a brief and complete summary of spiritual doctrine, and more exactly the best commentary on the program: «Reaching out toward the fullness of communion with the God of the Covenant, fulfillment of every hope».

Tuesday

TC pp. 222-225, «It shall never be that… but humble and will be looking for me»

It shall never be that all the riches down here make me leave my Lord.

I rose to run, but the sores on my legs and body troubled me greatly. I entered a beautiful field, but very badly tilled; a gracious peasant woman came toward me and asked what was the matter with me. Oh! I almost did not want to say, but she again added:«Do you feel unwell?»

«No!»

Only at her insistence did I tell her that I had certain sores on my legs and feet that would not let me walk. She looked at me with compassion.

«Come into my farmhouse; I have a certain ointment that will heal you.»

I looked at her, and then gave another glance at my path, which in no way led to the farmhouse.

«Thank you! May God repay you for your charity, but I cannot stop.»

And I continued my way. At last, arriving near a brook, I sat down and meanwhile bathed my sores in that water. It came suddenly to my mind: Oh! my Crucified did not have this refreshment for his countless wounds, and must I have it for this one portion? I immediately gave up this refreshment, and walked on. Those sores that I had bathed and that burned me less I at once sought to aggravate with stinging herbs. And I always asked my God’s pardon for it.

I passed near a garden, magnificent for its flowers, graceful in design; on every side fine coats of arms could be seen and every so often a guard. My path led right into one of these. As soon as I entered I found myself lost in so much richness of trees and fruits.

A guard comes up to me and curtly asks where I am going, and tells me not to delay leaving, because wanderers could not enter there. What to do? I tried to persuade him, but there was no reason that could convince him. My path was that one and I could not leave it.

«In the name of my Lord, let me pass!»

«No! turn back!»

Then I said to him:

«It shall never be that I do this, because I have orders to come here.

«Who are you?» he asked me.

I am a slave of the Lord who sent me here.

While the dispute went on, I commended myself to my God to turn my path aside. No! A great Lady arrives, all dressed in brocade; with her she had a large dog; and yet she comes up to me and tells me to turn back, making a sign of using force and driving me away. My Crucified! you were thus driven away by Annas!

«Let me go on! I promise not to harm you in anything, but I will pass through in haste.»

«No!»

They goad the dog to drive me away. Nothing! the beast does not move. The woman wanted to give me alms and told me that I moved her to great compassion.

«Thank you! I have no need of alms, because my Lord is very rich and lets me lack nothing. Ah! let me pass!»

Moved to compassion, she looked me over from head to foot and then begged me to sit down, for she wanted to speak to me.

«Your charity and kindness in all that you ask of me would deserve my compliance, but I cannot: night is falling and I must withdraw.

With a compassionate act she gave me leave to pass, telling the guard to accompany me. All at once I find her close to me again:

«Stop!»

«No!»

«If you stay with me I assure you I will make you happy. Do you see?»

«It shall never be that all the riches and beauties down here make me leave my Lord.»

«Oh! who then is this Lord of yours?»

«You will know Him, but you will not possess Him.»

«What heresies!» said the woman ù This is an ignorant bigot: let her go!

So I remained free and, running, I thought: poor wretch: she does not know my God! What a pain! And praying much and weeping, I asked the Lord to give light to that poor woman, who caused me so much pain. After so much prayer, my voice:

«Your prayers will be heard and you will see the woman again, no longer proud but humble, and she will be looking for me. (45).

Wednesday

TC pp. 450-453, «A most noble lady… with his fiery persecutions!»

A most noble lady, benefactress of the Work of God.

Amid the most terrible anguish on a journey undertaken, I was warned by a holy creature that at the very point where I had to pass there were evildoers who had planned to harm me. But it was God’s will that I pass that way. Fear and anxiety invaded me. Arriving at the place, (the fear) vanished from my mind and finally, reassured, after a very long stretch, I found myself at the place where God had sent me.

After two days that I had been living in that farmhouse, a gracious matron came. On meeting her, I at once felt something in me I cannot name. Who is she?

My voice: - A most noble lady who will do much good for my brides.

- Oh my Love! she is married and young: how?

Nothing more did I receive. Several times I saw her and felt toward her a certain confidence; and I told her many things about the Work of the Lord. I left that delightful farmhouse and stayed a long time without seeing her again; but in thought I seemed always to have her near.

I had to return to that field and more than the first time we found ourselves close; and I told her much of how I found myself in this field, that it was all the work of my Master and had been created by his Vicar on earth, and that I was only the poor slave and good for nothing; that He alone worked, and that so great was my incapacity and ignorance that many times I undid what He had done. And I tried to make her understand well how ignorant I was. But the lady was not put off by my state, but on the contrary took pleasure in the work and in the fine labor that God was making delightful gardens spring up. Each day this matron grew in affection for the Work and I saw clearly the labor that the divine Majesty was doing in that upright, simple heart, so great in loving.

She desired to have offspring and I prayed much that the holy Mother would obtain it for her. Once I deceived myself with this answer that I heard: - She will have more than one!

Oh! I rejoiced; but when I had the explanation, that they were not natural, but spiritual (those daughters), there arose in me something mixed regarding her soul: I rejoiced, but at the thought that materially she would suffer I felt sorrow. And then I went on thinking: how can it be that she remains at the head of a field when she is so well accompanied? How many prayers and struggles did I have to sustain!

Meanwhile one could see that her heart was bending wholly toward the Work of the Lord and that the labor of the mystical Gardener was gaining ground, and that that heart could no longer have anything more tasty to satisfy it.

She works and, like one of the most zealous laborers, with her whole person attends to the fields. Very intelligent, endowed with a very lofty mind and sound judgment, as soon as she was able to enter fully into a matter, she promptly forms an exact judgment and is very firm in her resolutions. But how to describe the nobility of her heart? She was endowed with such a gentle feeling that for all she had the greatest charity. She preferred to undergo every privation and even renounced certain persons dear to her, provided she knew she was doing a favor and satisfying in any way the pleasure of others, sacrificing herself. And this came so easily to her, in appearance, that one would have thought her indifferent, whereas I can assure you she was quite otherwise. Finally she sets her hand to another, more beautiful work: she prepares a great building to put in it certain creatures who must learn to cultivate the fields well and meanwhile, in their solitude, will praise God and strive to serve Him as best they can. What will she have from God? The graces of the Lord have no end. Oh! blessed are you who have so well answered the voice of the Lord!

Her thoughts, her anxieties are all for the Work of God; she rejoices at the thought of her beautiful and graceful field, where she so anxiously desires to see the plants soon grow. But the dragon, powerful enemy of so fine and beautiful a plantation, rages, stirs up disputes and weaves plots so that it may not be realized. Horror! how fiercely he clings on every side!

But the mighty hand of God (will not fail); I see clearly from this farmhouse that his efforts are stones thrown into the water. Oh! beautiful work of omnipotence, so that that beautiful field may be purified and have strong foundations! Let the enemy harden its soil, fertilize it with his fiery persecutions!».

Thursday

TC pp. 403-405, «My voice commands me… carry out your orders»

My voice commands me to run, and all persecute me because I run too much

My voice:

- It is time to advance in the fields and with courage to sow!

- My God, your slave is ready!

Running thus, at every moment I met people, and pastors who bothered me, telling me that I ran too much in sowing, that the harvest would not be at all fine. Finally to these were added also great pastors, who grumbled a great deal. A certain panic took hold of me and I was almost about to slow down the work.

My voice:

- Oh! what are you doing?

Without paying further heed I began to run harder still. Oh! what happened to me! A superior of the pastors stops me, abuses me and with unkind insults says that I am proud and that I see nothing else but the satisfaction of having fields to give vent to my pride, that I only aim at having estates and fields.

Oh! how I felt my chest tighten: as between two very large stones I felt it being crushed. I went saying to myself: how should I behave? my voice does not err, and yet it is always the one that commands me to run; and all persecute me because I run more than anything; with these join also the women workers, my companions, who grumble and complain because I make them work too much; not only that, but that it pains them to see my continual walking without giving myself respite, that I rush too much. They do not at all admit this way of mine. And several times they say to me:

- It is time to stop and put things in order, so as not to have to scourge yourself so much in this way.

My God! what to do? Is the voice that commands me to run not yours? Perhaps that ugly one is trying to deceive me?

How I had to struggle! Humanity joined itself to what these said: it took up the whole part and associated itself perfectly with them, and would gladly have put into practice what they said, that is, to stop. Thus besieged, I begged God to take me out of so painful a state. Was I mistaken? Weeping with my face to the ground I lay.

My voice:

- These speak humanly. Forward, follow me!

Oh my Love! your slave wants nothing else but to carry out your orders perfectly!

Friday

FS pp. 253-254, «Her spirituality of the sick… I felt I did everything»

Her spirituality of the sick and the poor derived from faith in the affirmation of Jesus: Whatever you did for one of these least of my brothers, you did for me (Mt 25:40) (cf. Circ. Letter year 1876).

This faith had been at the beginning of her new life, in 1858, a true experience, similar to that of St. Francis of Assisi when he kissed the leper, overcoming his repugnance, and then found sweet what before was bitter to him. Rosa kissed the ulcers of the sick and sometimes even passed her tongue over them (FIOCCHI, I, p. 43).

Having found Jesus in the suffering, it was sweeter for her to contemplate the wounded Redeemer himself. One night, tired after a day wholly taken up in service to the sick, she had a rapture, in which she experienced the consolation of sucking the wound in the Lord’s shoulder: returning to herself, she felt completely invigorated (M 1.1, p. 59f). Another time, in 1864, after a similar experience contemplating the Passion of the Lord, she wrote:

«My soul remained so strengthened that, returning to my work, I felt neither pain nor the odor of my sick. It was sweet to serve them and in my God I felt I did everything» (M 2, p. 107).

Saturday

Tr. pp. 41-42, «Walk before me… the way with word and deeds

Walk before me and be perfect» (Gen 17:1). Here lies the substance of the spirituality of the old covenant. St. Anne practiced this principle in the most perfect manner, she walked in the presence of God, and when one walks continually before the gaze of God who reads in the depths of the soul, then one walks toward holiness and toward an ever greater perfection. In this sense St. Anne too grew from day to day in holiness until she was ready for the extraordinary mission that God would entrust to her. It was this extraordinary holiness that made her worthy mother of the Immaculate One, and perfect anticipated model of the holiness lived and preached by Jesus. In this sense she is not only a culminating point of the holiness and spiritual perfection of the old Covenant, but a concrete anticipation of the spiritual perfection lived and preached by Jesus. The bond between the holiness of the mother of the Immaculate One and that of the new Covenant lies wholly here. St. Anne therefore lived a solid and prayerful faith, substantiated by hope in the expectation of the day of the Lord: come, come, O blessed Messiah, come to save and redeem your people, come O desired of the nations who chose Israel for yourself as your chosen people and almost beloved son. Come to soothe the suffering longing for your sensible and beneficent presence. Come to enlighten our way with word and deeds (cf. Rule 1869, p. 14).

13th Sunday in Ordinary Time

TC pp. 368-371, «A group of creatures… and to live and die for Him alone.»

A group of creatures guided by a pastor of good zeal, but inept.

They rushed off and I saw them no more. Still, the waters of the river made a way for me. On a delightful day I was climbing the mountain gently. When I was halfway I met certain creatures all dressed in uniform. They were alone. I stopped them and asked where they were going. With arrogance they answer me:

- Where we like!

- Very well, dear creatures. Forgive me if I have been too bold; but I know that on these roads there are evildoers and that, being so alone, you will meet with fear and could come to real trouble.

They stop and say to me:

- Who are you?

- Dear creatures - I answered - I am a poor slave.

- Oh! how? - they said - in these parts of ours we have no slaves.

- What are you saying? - I answered them - I don’t believe it! A little squabble followed, curious in itself. Annoyed, one of them said: - Whose slave are you?

- My God’s.

- Ah! we understand: she must be a bigot, a companion of our pastor!

- What are you saying! - I added - Where do you have this pastor? And they paint me a picture of him in their own way: they call him a cretin, ignorant, good for nothing but praying.

- Oh! fine! - I added - how? does he not give you instruction? does he not make you sociable creatures? From what I see in you, your spirit would tend toward family and society. A pity!

And here she made me see that she was wholly of their party. Meanwhile I wanted to go on my way unconcerned; but these, eager to hear me speak and seeing themselves heeded, begged me to let them accompany me.

- Yes - I answered them - gladly, so we can talk about something beautiful. Meanwhile would you kindly tell me whether your dwelling is far.

They answered me that it was near.

But are you alone?

- Oh! we were many, but because of that bigot!… If you knew what has happened…

- Oh! tell me, and if I can be of service in anything I will do so gladly.

My God, help me! I repeated to myself. How many horrible things they did! and these too were headed to look for another shelter that might please them more. That poor pastor was truly a good soul, but what he wanted to do was not called by God, but he worked only out of zeal; he lacked the compass to navigate. And they kept on telling me. Every now and then I interrupted them to learn what was in their minds.

- Here - they tell me - we shall be there shortly.

And they beg me to sit down, because they want to tell me everything. I agree. When they had finished their sorrowful and indecent story, I began to say to them:

- Tell me frankly: if that shelter took another form and were provided with good persons who would impart to you science and doctrine, would you be happy to stay?

- Surely, we would be most happy, oh! - all continued to say - and we will believe there is a God.

- Oh! poor me! what are you saying? - I added.

- You must know - so they - that it is despair that forces us to speak this way.

I rise and say to them:

- Well then: promise to follow me and behave well, and I will put you in a position to be good and educated, so that you may earn your bread and live honestly.

All kneel and make protests of obedience and submission.

- Tell us, - they say to me - and how will you manage with that pastor?

- Leave the care and the action to me, to you the steadfastness. And we set out toward that house.

I found that pastor weeping, because all had fled from him and only (there remained) an old guardian woman, who was grumbling with all her might. This poor man, on seeing me together with these his fled little sheep, blessed me and left everything in my power to do and undo. I sent the old woman away and kept the promise I had made to these runaways, who were not long in leaving the thought of the fine world and, trampling everything underfoot, learned to love God and to live and die for Him alone.

Monday

TC pp. 363-364, «Diversity of God’s love… do you speak of love?»

I would never have left this temple; but it was his will that I leave. So, without further remark, I set out. After walking two hours and more, here is what the voice had told me. Oh magnificence! it was something delightful. I went into fields of various and diverse flowers; so many graceful girls vied to offer them to me. I accepted many; but I always kept in mind the word: «You will find flowers and laurel to weave». What must I do? - I went saying to myself. And these kept bringing me more. There was laurel. One of them, older and bolder, said to me:

- See all these fields, how beautiful they are and so full of flowers!

- Yes - I answered her.

- Well, for not knowing how to weave them, once gathered they wither and become foul-smelling.

- Oh! - I added - Why do you not try to give them to Jesus?

- You tell us how we should do it.

- Let us make a garland and give it to that church which has a field attached, but a poor one; the farmhouse where the poor women workers are is so dilapidated that those poor women live there miserably.

These creatures were listening to me.

- Well! - they said to me - weave as many as you like, take them to those creatures, thus for the church you speak of.

I was not long in setting to work. And they helped me with great pleasure. How happy I felt, because I was doing great things with those bunches. I took a quantity of laurel.

- This - I said - is for you, who with such generosity help the poor and the brides of the Lord, as well as his church. You will be crowned with laurel for eternity. And I shall strive to weave it so well, putting into it all the ability my Master will give me.

One of these, who more than the others had been silent, comes up to me and says:

- Could I too not learn together with you the same lessons that your Master gives you?

- Oh! yes, certainly! He - I began to say - is all for all, and rejoices greatly when a creature shows herself eager to learn. Yes, come with me and you will see how you will learn to weave roses and lilies… I forgot the laurel: more than anything my Jesus cares for this, and how graceful is its weaving!

Without thinking, carried away by joy, I exclaimed: My Love! My Love! Enchanted, she said to me:

- But how is it that until now you told us that you are alone and a slave of the Lord.

- And it is true what you say - I answered her - Is He not my God, my Love?

- What? - this one resumed, as if I had blasphemed - do you speak of love?

Tuesday

TC pp. 268-271, «She finds mute children… And mute I went along the road»

She finds mute children: she takes them with her to feed them and make them know God

Only on recovering did I find myself in a delightful garden, where there were a few children. I asked them who they were and whose that beautiful place was. They did not answer. Perhaps they are mute? And I tried to make myself understood by signs. I was not mistaken: they were poor abandoned creatures, seeking shelter. What compassion they stirred in me! I took them with me, because they had knocked long at that palace, but no one had listened to them. All joyful they skipped around me. I thought at once that they were hungry. Turning to my God: what can I give these creatures, I who have nothing? what must I do? Taking off my cloak and approaching a woman who had much bread, I begged her to accept my cloak and give me bread for these creatures I had found along this road. The good woman looked at me and, taking the cloak, gave me plenty of bread. Having distributed this to the poor creatures, I looked for where I could find a stream to give them to drink; I see in the distance a little girl with an amphora heading toward us. Oh! what pleasure I felt (and they) no less than mine. I realized that these poor creatures were burning with thirst and rejoiced to be able to have water. Who sends you, dear creature? As soon as she was near us, she sets down her amphora and invites us to drink. For all the questions I asked her, I could never understand who had sent her and who she was. She took back her vessel and, with extraordinary speed, flew away, for more than a walk one can say (it was) a flight.

These poor creatures were tired, and where to let them rest? My voice:

- A few steps more and you will find shelter for these creatures. So it happened. To an old woman, seated on a stone, I asked whether she would do me the charity of lodging these creatures. Grumbling she looks at me:

- I have only one bed and this is for me!

- Tell me, do you not have straw?

Unwillingly she points me to a hayloft, which I accepted at once. And as best I could I put these creatures to sleep. But, once they were asleep, I began to pray and weep: what shall I give these poor little ones tomorrow? My God, I feel torn apart!

As soon as (day broke), I went to the woman, who was already grumbling around the hearth. I begged her to give me bread for the poor little ones who were sleeping. What did I do? I took off my skirts and gave them to her, so that she would give me bread. She became cheerful, accepted the skirts and gave me plenty of bread and fruit. How happy I was! I looked at the basket with great satisfaction; those poor creatures came to meet me skipping and at once I put the basket at their disposal and they were satisfied. The rest I took and we set out along the path.

How shall I be able to teach these mute creatures to love God and make Him known to them? Thinking thus, I looked at them and felt great compassion. I heard a bell, and the more we ran the nearer we came to it. It was a graceful little village with civilized people; I asked a young woman where the church was:

- I hear ringing and I do not understand where the temple is.

She told me that there are certain good souls who have mute little girls. I cannot express what I felt! Arriving at these, I begged them to accept the poor little ones I had with me. They were not slow to grant my request; but the pain on both sides at having to part was something…! But they must learn to know God! My voice: - One day you will see them again. On Calvary Jesus is found! And mute I went along the road.

Wednesday

D. pp. 63-64, «In 1862, in a period of struggle… it is sweet to die with Jesus»

In 1862, in a period of struggle with the evil one, Jesus enlightens her about the discernment of spirits, making her pass through a painful but liberating experience. An experience that confirms her regarding the power of Christ over her life and above all his power over the evil one, whose vexations she must not fear. It enlightens her about the meaning of certain diabolical actions.

Thus she recounts this phase of liberation: «…he (the devil) came out with new inventions, but my Director knew well how to find a way to make me feel with my own hand that nothing would happen at the hour of my death and so on, whatever else the dragon whispered to me» (M. 1.1, p. 28).

Finding herself alone she felt ill, but nothing happened to her of what the devil had whispered to her. Once the illness passed, the Voice of Jesus intervenes:

«…now you will believe that they are all temptations, but that it was not enough for you to have seen everything cancelled, and he adds yet another reproach. Oh, what pains I felt! But I always went on thinking of the peace of that moment when I fainted… How sweet it is to die with Jesus…» (M. 1.1, p. 29).

Thursday

TC pp. 239-241, «Battered and scourged… he vows to trouble us always»

Battered and scourged on all sides, I begged my Father for mercy and pity. I had nothing on which to lean in an arid field with only sharp thorns: so they had reduced me. And they were full of joy over the victory won. My mind could no longer have a point on which to rest.

Drained of strength, I threw myself to the ground in the midst of these terrible thorns, but the pain was without equal. So your work will be destroyed by such fierce evildoers? And weeping face down on the ground I kept making loud laments. Will everything be lost? My voice:

«Rise! Never will my work have to suffer for it, it will triumph ever more!»

I sat on the ground and was still weeping when I see all my hands bloodied and with great pains in my knees, which also had certain sharp thorns in them. What to do? On every side where I turned my gaze I saw nothing but the same field, whose end I could not see; and so arid! only dry thorn bushes that kept me from moving, because I felt horrible stings. There was no longer any trace of a road, not even among these terrible points. Where am I? Will there be no more hope for me of leaving here? My God! have pity on your slave! why have you condemned me so terribly? I know that my negligences in your service unfortunately deserve worse; but I am dying of sorrow for having displeased you; my chest is breaking with grief, my hands and body are all stings! Oh! my God! I know too well that this loathsome body is the cause of my having lost you.

At this thought, I rose and gathered a good number of these thorns, and with all my strength set about fiercely beating myself.

My voice:

«Stop!» it cried to me.

And fainting I abandoned myself to the ground. How long I stayed I do not know. I heard a voice, so sweet, that said to me:

«My beloved, rise!»

And as if He had taken me by the hand. I opened my eyes:

«Oh! my Love! I have no more life!»

He answered me:

«Do you not have mine?»

Oh! with what boldness I rose! Kneeling I did not dare stand up; I begged Him with hands joined not to leave me any more in this devastated field, where I was led by people who have done so much harm to your (slave).

«Take me with you, I can no longer stay down here!

«There is still too much time» He signaled to me; and vanished.

And I, seated on the ground, looked at my wounds, in which I no longer felt the slightest pain. Night was drawing near.

«My Good, you have left me alone here! Is there no path to go out?

So saying, I rose. Here is my path! After a few steps, no more thorns, but beautiful! it was a delight of paradise. I met a gracious young woman and she wanted to stop me to tell me…: what? I feared to stop, but (I had) a desire to hear. The first word she said to me was:

«Rejoice, for those persecutors have been mocked and put to flight. They left the field; and you will see it again far more beautiful than before.

I said to her:

«Do me the charity of coming with me to tell me.

The gracious young woman obliged me and along the way told me all that had happened to them: while they believed themselves victorious, a person came who was well informed and brought everything to light, and full of shame they went away. One, however, the fiercest, said he would never give up his opinion and that he vows to trouble us always.

Friday

FS pp. 167-168, «The sufferings of the spirit… let us pray strongly»

The sufferings of the spirit

Endowed with great sensitivity, she could not remain indifferent to the situations of others, especially when it concerned persons to whom she felt more bound. Let us recall her sufferings because of her children and her brother Federico. Nothing afflicted her like the sense of the offense against God. She wrote in 1890 to her friend the Princess of Fitalia: «Dear Emilia, I feel my chest breaking with grief, thinking how dear Jesus is offended and by whom he is offended. I do not know what I would do; I feel a courage that, were it not for God, our sweet Love, where I would go I do not know. Let us leave it, and pray strongly» (28-5-1890).

Saturday

TC pp. 372-373, «The God of mercies is… of so immense a treasure»

The God of mercies is a most severe judge.

20 January 1892.

Absorbed in deep meditation on the Passion of my Lord, I passed in flight to God’s mercy toward man. I found myself engulfed and felt wholly compressed, as if in that abyss every fault were to be dispersed: I rejoiced! When suddenly the view changed to the justice of God. How to describe this? The smallest imperfections are written and pictured before me. The God of mercies is a most severe judge! I trembled from head to foot; a strong inner agitation made me unable to find my way back to mercy. No! wretched me! Forgetful of anything created and of myself, I thought of one thing only and this occupied all my mental faculties: my Love the Judge! I felt myself shudder all over and wept strongly. My voice:

- Why do you let yourself be carried away so meanly?

Full of shame I asked God’s pardon and I always thought how mercy, for one who loves, surpasses justice (cf. Jas 2:13). Weary, I fell asleep; but it was so brief, because as soon as I fell asleep a voice woke me saying it was time to pray, certain souls being very fiercely tempted. What can it be? Thrown to the ground, I prayed to God with all the strength of my soul and made fervent vows that the Lord would free those creatures from the devil’s snares, and command those ugly ones to depart. And, to prevent them from consenting, I began to scourge myself so that, by my mortifying the flesh, they might remain free and not stay prey to those terrible dragons.

This done, I fell into a prostration of strength and had to abandon myself to the ground. In those sufferings I enjoyed a great consolation: it was union with my God. Meanwhile, one of these poor creatures - who was surely her angel - said to me:

- Thank you! through you we are freed; from God you will have the reward.

And she added that she already possessed so immense a treasure.

14th Sunday in Ordinary Time

TC pp. 485-487, «Sweet Love! I served you badly… to my hand and vanished»

Sweet Love! I served you badly by mistaking the path!

Thus resigned, I ran; but a deep sadness held me bound: all my mental faculties tied up, I was like a senseless woman who walks, not knowing where and not even realizing she is tired, a true donkey that goes, goes, as long as its legs hold and then throws itself on the ground. So it happened to this slave of yours. Shaken by weariness, I realized that I was in a wood thick with trees: a sepulchral silence! My God, where am I? who led me here? My voice: - Your carelessness!

How is it that, without noticing, I find myself in so terrible a labyrinth? My God, pity! Ah! my Master, my Lord, mercy on my fault! And I repeated to myself: so I have been careless! Alas, what have I done? I threw myself on the ground among those plants: My Lord! I deserve nothing else but to be devoured by beasts. I understand: I do not deserve mercy or pardon; let the vipers of this frightening wood devour me and I, resigned, will bear the penalty. Oh! what have I done? And that melancholy, which always accompanies me, I felt it destroying me. Oh! I offended you, sweet Love! Yes, I served you badly by mistaking the path, and here I am! I took hold of certain thorn bushes and with all my strength beat this donkey, because through its fault I had committed such carelessness; and I wept bitterly. A light all at once (appears to me) and I feel myself seized by the arm and told: - Enough!

Oh! my angel! Prostrate with hands joined, which were bloodied, I told him weeping that I had committed that carelessness and that surely my Lord had been displeased and that I deserved nothing else but to be devoured by the beasts.

He looked at me and, smiling, lifted me up.

- Ah! why, my dear guide, did you allow me to stray from the path?

He did not answer me. He looked at my hands and at the ground where the blood was, and then said to me: - This had to be shed for the good of certain fields that you will have to set in order. Dry your tears and come with me.

He took me by the hand and led me out of that wood. A beautiful light brightened my path and it was clearer than day itself.

- Do not leave me! - every minute I said to him; and I held his hand tightly - But tell me truly: is my Lord no longer displeased with me?

- No: very dear to Him are your protests, your anxieties and fears.

- But I suffer greatly! it is the agony of death!

- Everything is acceptable to Him and He takes pleasure in it.

Having said this, he gave my hand a squeeze, and vanished.

Monday

TC pp. 338-342, «Accused before a judge… that bends badly «

Accused before a most severe judge, who treats her harshly, because of a woman worker.

While I was reasoning thus, my voice interrupts me, commanding me to go where certain unknown people were molesting a flock of good and innocent lambs, and wanted to rob several. Without further thought I leave everything and set out where I saw the way traced for me. Arriving where these wretched people truly were, as if I had come from a sumptuous banquet, I set about driving those ugly ones away and putting the flock back in order, by changing its guard and giving it a faithful keeper.

While I stood still, leaning on a stone, I was strongly rebuked by very eminent persons; and one of them sent me to a most severe judge who, ill-informed, abused me horribly, over certain accusations that, truly, I do not know where they could have got them. For some moments I remained mute, and then I begged him to be patient and listen to me; but it was something curious: all because they were defending a woman worker who had barbarously withdrawn from the field and was strongly protected by the pastors.

This ended, I went to another, and yet from him, rudely, I received certain answers…! My God! - I went saying - it is nothing compared to what you suffered!

At last, weary, I returned to my poor farmhouse and, thrown on the ground weeping, begged mercy of my God. Everything was for me of dark bronze, in perfect darkness I walked and found new stumbling blocks, oppressed by a thousand sorrows.

A summons from another pastor, that I should go to that judgment. And so, running, I set out. But what a surprise! The unhappy victorious woman was leaving the judge and strutting among her protectors. I huddled under a portico and stood all trembling. I forced myself and prayed to my Crucified to help me, because I felt I was fainting. Arriving with difficulty before the judge, oh! how I trembled! The slanders, the horrible inventions I heard! My God! how will this so cruel persecution end? I no longer even knew how to answer, because they were of a curious entanglement. And he left me free, telling me that he would come together with others to defend that unhappy woman. It was not long in coming true; and first a pastor came with a world of fictions; he wanted to make me believe certain invented falsehoods, that the acts he performed were of unequaled exaggeration; he wanted to annihilate himself with the protests he made; he would have wished to persuade me that for me he would sacrifice anything.

The next day what was my surprise! he was together with the other judges and, entirely changed in character, but fierce, as never before he insulted me in a quite singular way; he had the backing of the others and gave himself great strength. The unhappy woman was brought before them, crowned with laurels and perfectly acquitted, satisfied in all she desired, and they condemned me. Oh! my sweet Love! Then indeed I was content, thinking that you too, my God, were put after Barabbas! And with joy I stood before the judges, full of consolation, offering them my miserable service in the small refreshment they took. Within me I was happy. My dear Crucified! they only condemned me to give what they thought, but I was not condemned to death like you. They insulted me and I tried to imitate you by doing her good.

One of these, after several days, returned to my poor farmhouse and asked my pardon, telling me to forget what he had done to me. Oh! never, my God! To you no one came to ask forgiveness, neither Annas nor Caiaphas nor Pilate, and why do you allow them to ask it of me?

But the struggle was not yet over, because the others still tried to oppress me, especially one who was very fierce. At last his turn came, and he could vent himself at his pleasure and left me in a very bad state with his ill-treatment. He took flight, shouting all the while. I had been left spellbound; the people who saw him so furious were also left spellbound and asked one another: what is he doing? for what reason? Other women workers wept and I tried to lift them up with jokes and laughter, thinking that he must have needed to vent himself and that, if it was good for him, it was good too that it happened. My voice:

A day will come when you must do good to this one who persecutes you so; but he will always remain hard of heart. He believes that no one does better than he; he persuades himself and lives convinced.

I suffered much on seeing how he treated the poor women workers, even more the vineyard of the Lord: he always despised it as if only weeds had been born there; he saw the fruits and I can say he tasted them, judging them excellent, and then he would never give it any help. If this happened, it was all the work of his master who, grateful, wanted at least to bless some of those large fields; but this one always dragged him away and sought every invention to keep him far off. What terrible aversion! One can never come to believe that in this land of toil there can be creatures so ungrateful for the good received; and yet, in the vast field of the Lord there unfortunately are. My voice, while I reasoned:

- And how many I had when I preached to my ungrateful people!

I stopped to think and weigh well these holy words and, after a long while, I answered:

- Oh! how I must always complain!

I almost felt in me a certain displeasure because I could not manage to obtain that all should respond to the great benefits of the Lord. I began to say:

- My God, how should I behave?

My voice:

- Always do as much good as possible to your neighbor, without caring whether they will respond or not. Never judge and accuse your brother of ingratitude: always try to excuse all the actions of others. Take with you a good woman worker and go to that field, where some plant that bends badly needs straightening.

Tuesday

TC pp. 519-521, «Always ready for sacrifice… your orders carried out!»

While I thought I had traveled enough valleys and cliffs and rivers and sea, seized by extreme weakness, leaning on a trunk that I thought strong, I stopped, sure of regaining my strength. The trunk weakens, collapses, I see it fail me. An agitation invades me, every hour I see myself engulfed. Where to save myself? Turning to the wonder-worker of Paola for help, I prayed to him strongly: he was of bronze! Turning to another protectress of mine, with strong weeping, I sent her supplications that she might save me. She answered me in a firm tone:

- I have thought of it.

But meanwhile the trunk was crumbling more and more; by all appearances not the slightest support was to be hoped for from it any longer. Crying out I called my angel. I am lost! What I saw became frightening to me. And weeping I clung to the foot of the cross, while my strength was reduced to a minimum. My angel seized me by an arm and, shaking me from so horrible a lethargy, gave me strength and, pointing out to me a long and sorrowful road that awaited me, said to me:
