- Go! God sends you there: you will have much to suffer, but you will be sustained by the strength of the Lord.

I looked at him and weeping said to him:

- Ah! promise me to be always with me.

And he:

- Am I not always near you?

- No! - I said to him.

And he, smiling at me always:

- I will be with you, do not fear! The dragon will not move under my foot. You will have to struggle with every sort of people; they will want to stop you on the way, and even one who is with you will exhort you to turn back. Woe to you if you heed the human claws that will be raised up to frighten you.

I look at the road and feel myself invaded by horrible dread; as in a flash my mind is terrified. My angel notices this disturbance of mine and in a stern tone says to me:

- Think of fulfilling the will of God: woe to you if you turn back!

And he vanished.

Mute, my forehead resting on my hand, I stood motionless. After a long while I resumed:

- Where is the strength, my Crucified, to do all you command me? This poor slave of yours is always ready for sacrifice under the yoke of work: she will never dare to stop! (Your orders) will be carried out!

Wednesday

D. pp. 110-111, The Spirit and the mission… it seemed to encircle my head»

The Holy Spirit, whom the Father reveals through his mission in time: in creation, in the word of the Prophets, in the Incarnation of the Word in Mary’s womb, in the life of the Son and in his work, in the proclamation and work of the Apostles after the glorification of Jesus, fully manifests the fullness of the Trinitarian mystery and continues his work in the mission of the Church.

His mission unfolds from then on in the children adopted by the Father in Christ Jesus.»

The life and mission of Rosa, as daughter in the Son, are therefore a mystical place of the Presence and mission of the Spirit.

Her «time» - the stretch of history entrusted by the Father to her - was a time of the Spirit and of witness, but also a time marked by various needs and by trials that did not spare her, a time of vigilance and trusting expectation.

On every page of her Memoirs the presence of the Spirit in her life and mission is attested:

«…but He who governs and works in this very work of His, knows well how to take away and give as He pleases… the mental illuminations became much clearer and more alive to me, so that, to my amazement, I feel such sublime words coming out of my mouth, and I find everything easy: to preach, to explain and to resolve anything that is asked of me…» (M. 3, p. 1).

And on another page she continues the description of this mystical Presence in her life and mission, which turns out to be a marvelous interweaving of the work of the Spirit and of her participation:

«I feel, and more clearly I see myself guided by my dear Spirit…»;

«I was always working, but did not know how or why I worked… I did everything, not I, but the One who lives in me: I felt that I answered and did not know what. I saw everything proceeding in order and did not know who ordered it. I, in truth, was not capable because… a tight crown seemed to encircle my head…» (M. 3, pp. 11; 13).

Thursday

TC pp. 465-467, «Comforted and instructed by the… he signed my forehead and vanished»

My angel said to me:

- Stop! turn back: look where you are! Horrible sight! I look and, from the fright received from such ugly people who were carousing, I gave a loud cry and held tight to my angel’s sword. I look around and, alas, nothing is seen but cliffs. He took me by the hand, and in a flash I found myself in a soft park, I say soft because of thick grass, barely ten centimeters high: it seemed I was walking on velvet.

My angel cast a glance at my feet, which were bleeding, and with this grass I was healed. And he left me, while I hoped he would tell me many things; and the more I wished to hear something of my God: nothing! Thus mortified I sat down on that grass and, weeping bitterly, said:

- Why leave me so? at least one word… So I must have done wrong in going into that thicket: that carelessness of mine, surely, not pleasing my Master, it will no longer be given me to see Him, Oh! my Crucified! ah! speak to me, if you do not want to see me die of grief! It is a horrible pain: speak to me!

And I cried at the top of my voice. The grief became so strong that I fainted abandoned on the ground: I no longer felt anything nor was I capable of understanding. A hand shakes me saying:

- My beloved, look at me, for I am always with you!

Oh surprise! My Good! my Master! I knelt prostrate and He gave me a sweet liquor to drink.

- Rise! I have many things to tell you. Who could describe what I felt? A long lesson He gave me: how I was to cultivate certain new fields I would have and the way I was to conduct myself with the pastors who were in those fields, and what would happen to me. When I heard that so much suffering was being prepared for me, I interrupted Him:

- My God! will you always be with me?

He smiled at me, and then:

- With you I always am!

A strong trembling took me when I heard terrible sufferings and entanglements of things. And He, pressing my hand, said to me:

- Do not fear! you have my strength and only with this can you bear this.

He signed my forehead and vanished.

Friday

FS pp. 139-140, «She declares herself several times… death of love, how sweet and tasty you are»

She declares herself several times a slave for love of her beloved Good. Painful absences are not lacking, in which she feels as if forgotten, unworthy even of a glance from the God of Love; but suddenly she feels near, sweetly drawn by Him, and hears in her inmost depths his voice reassuring her of his love and saying to her: «You are my beloved» (M 4.4, p. 76f).

When she experiences such assurance, everything becomes easy for her, every pain desirable:

«Your love, my Good, surpasses everything and is the support, the relief, the security of acting. It is the anchor that holds at the bottom of the painful sea of our tribulations. Most lovable God, when in the midst of such sad suffering you leave us anchored in your love, it is enough to say to the pains: You are sweet, O my beloved! And the fear of having displeased you is followed by trust in your pardon, the assurance of soon having clarifications in the rest of our actions and, finally, the blessedness of your perfect union which, by means of love, is always tasted, though in more or less intimacy» (M 4.2, p. 89).

Often she finds herself unable to declare the ineffable experiences of infused love. At other times she feels as if invaded, dominated, subdued under the sweet violence of Love. And then her cry is: Love, how strong you are! which echoes that of the Song of Songs (Song 8:6). Thus on 9 April 1877: «I felt great union with my God, to such a degree that my ribs were so raised that I thought I would die under so fierce an anguish. Love, how strong you are! When I feel thus, I go saying: it is nothing! It is so strong, to such a degree that, if my Lover did not sustain me, I would die…; I already feel myself expiring when I feel thus. Oh! death of love, how sweet and tasty you are!» (M 4.4, p. 131f).

Saturday

TC pp. 487-490, «A portion of the labors… but at least she will be relieved»

Oh! - I cried out loudly - here I am alone! and where am I going? My voice:

- Behind the light that guides you!

I already felt faint, but I did not want to stop, because the light indicated it so. Meanwhile it seemed to me from moment to moment that I would fall to the ground and I begged my Lord to send me my angel, because I felt myself fainting. Behold, the light no longer points the way, but surrounds me on every side; I stop and it encircles me as if it held me enclosed within itself. I was near a graceful stone. I sat down; I felt myself strengthened, gathering a little strength; but the long fast, the weariness, everything I had gone through (kept me weighed down).

I was praying and waiting for I know not what: human relief certainly could not be had; but I do not know. I knew nothing, neither what to think nor how I should expect comfort. Wrapped in that light and seated I prayed. From the light itself came a graceful hand with a cup, and a voice that said to me: - Drink and you will be satisfied.

I drank. The light opened again and showed the way. And I, with a superhuman strength, ran. Meanwhile it could already be sensed a little that dawn would soon come. My mind went over everything that had happened. A poor soul, who a few hours before had passed into eternity, whispered to me to have prayers. So I thought to satisfy her desire; I would have wanted other signs from her, but in vain.

- But why do you always trouble me to have from me… - so the sentence remained suspended, because my voice (interrupted me):

- What you desire you will have, but there is still time.

She prays. Oh! dear soul, dear to God, blessed by my Lord forever! But other souls present themselves to me in an act of supplication. Oh! dear friends, what can I do for you? I am a poor slave and worse: yes, for from time to time I serve my Master poorly. I still feel the pain of a negligence committed: I was running heedlessly, and where did I find myself? This conversation took place along my way.

- And now, dear friends, see: I must walk, but I know neither where nor how I shall find a place to stop.

One answered me:

- It is very long, but it is very dear to God. Ah! offer for us a portion of these labors, so that we may soon be freed from so many pains.

I answered at once:

- Not a portion, but all this little bit that I am walking!

Oh! I hear a deep voice:

- And for me nothing? I have been condemned to darkness for so many years and only from you can I have light.

My God! this voice is not new to me. Oh! that soul!… Ah! let me see her. Behold, I see her: how she suffered! And what to do? The labor of that journey was offered by those; I felt deep sorrow at not being able to give this one relief at once. Oh! the charity of the just soul! The two souls I wanted to benefit present themselves promptly:

- Your suffering is too much; it is right that that soul have a portion of what you wanted to do for us and remain a sharer in the offering: gladly we yield the right.

- Oh charity! Thank you, dear friends! and I promise you that I will redouble my care until you have the fortune of seeing yourselves in the heavenly homeland.

Oh! how I felt true consolation!

- Well then, you burn to be able soon to enjoy Him who is all my longing, my only treasure, sweetest Master. Believe me, as much as you I feel what you feel of pain and sorrow, an inconceivable ardor to reach Him. Oh! once you are with my God, tell Him that I desire soon what I have asked of Him for so long. Ah! speak to Him of me, and then remember to come.

They draw near to me, and one says to me:

- For me there will still be much; I suffer much: see my pains!

Alas! a trembling seized me… Oh most merciful Savior! tell me what you want me to do for this poor soul: I offer myself to you to expiate her pains. My voice:

- Only in part do I allow it, because the journey is long and worse than what you suffer now you will have to suffer on arrival. I was shaken; but the sight of those pains was before me and I (had) a lively desire to relieve her. Well then, my Lord, let it be in part, but at least she will be relieved.

15th Sunday in Ordinary Time

TC pp. 99-101, «A fine future for the cultivation…. that it would end»

A fine future for the cultivation: there will be endless flourishing fields.

I was hesitating over what I should sow, when a person presents herself who (had) more the appearance of a heavenly creature than an earthly one, and thus in haste says to me to go with her, that they were about to devastate a field: many frosts had fallen and very dense fogs did not let the workers see where they were, and what had remained (was) clouded.

- How can I leave this land to help another?

- If you delay all is lost! - a voice insisting - No more reflections!

Together with that creature I set out to where one was running breathlessly. We passed through unknown people, but very barbarous, who had planned to kill me; but I passed without being recognized. Arrived at the place, a tumult of people: they wanted to seize the land. With a strong voice I ordered them to leave. But the plots, the vengeances they planned were something horrifying.

A soul so beautiful and sweet comes up to me; she assures me that those people roar, but they will be able to do nothing to me.

- Tell me, please, blessed soul, who sent you? Perhaps you are a heavenly messenger, and my God sent you here to defend His field? Tell me what you have kept in your heart.

At these words, spoken with great haste in order to have the answers, (she added):

- I have nothing more to tell you. And she remained sad.

- Why this sadness of yours? You have quite other things to tell me!

She comes up to me and, in an act of compassion, reasons about the future of my cultivation: that endless fields would flourish in it; and something beautiful in which my God took delight and with His visits made them fruitful, leaving them great treasures.

- Oh! how happy I would be to be able to find Him! For pity's sake, tell me in which field He is accustomed to go, for I want to find Him.

With an angelic smile she answered me that He is in the very field where I am, that it is not the workers who do much of that work, but the Lord Himself who brings the work to completion, giving it an exquisite beautification.

But I still did not feel satisfied with her speaking, and other sublime things I would have wanted her to tell me of my Good. But she fell asleep and, however much I asked her to wake, I could never obtain it. The thought came to me that it might not be sleep, but rapture; I fell silent and placed myself near her as if I could hear something. Prostrate on the ground I begged my God to let me (hear) a single instant. O goodness! drawing near, I heard the discourse; it was so beautiful! it described the future of two souls, and of one who was at the point of death: how beautiful she was! I did not notice that I was gradually becoming absorbed. An interweaving of sufferings of a new kind: the end was an Eden of delights! When it ended, we reasoned together and I would never have wanted it to end.

Monday

Tr. pp. 56-58, par. 3.3

The Church is truly the «people of God» to the extent that the baptized belong to Christ Jesus, to his mystical body. Precisely because the Church is identified with the «mystery hidden for ages in God», who is Jesus Christ, the reality of the Church, like that of Jesus, is the work of divine wisdom, and therefore it is immensely superior to our poor human concepts and to our capacity for understanding.

The Church is not only the «saved» people, the communion of believers, but also the «saving» universe.

Like Mary, the Church too brings forth human beings to a new and immortal life: this is her motherhood in the Holy Spirit (cf. RM 44). To suppose that the sinner as such belongs to her formally, and not virtually, leads one to think that the Church is sinful in full contrast with the «holy» Church. Not for nothing is it a mystery! The Church, born of the redeeming sacrifice of Christ and of the gift of the Holy Spirit, through the rite of baptism inserts us into Christ.

Baptism has always been the outward expression of faith, of incorporation and of conversion, that is, of the firm decision to renounce the past, sin, radically changing one's own mentality. Only on this condition does one come to be part of the people of God

The image of the Church as «people of God» must not therefore be isolated from the image of the Church as mystical body and immaculate bride of Christ, as in fact the Council does not isolate it. The Church as mystical body is a word inspired by the Holy Spirit and so Saint Paul proclaims it, and after him Tradition and the doctors of the Church, in particular Saint Augustine.

Only the image of the Church as mystical body allows us to understand that to separate oneself (through sin) from the Head is to separate oneself from the body that is the members. In this sense whoever separates from the Head separates from the members.

The image of the Church as «people of God» has the advantage of opening wide the door also to those who belong to her only virtually because all men, just as they have the vocation to Jesus Christ, head and king of humanity, so they have the vocation to the Church. In this sense also those who, through no fault of their own, do not know the Gospel and the Church, but live honestly, belong to the soul and not to the body of the Church. And if they live honestly according to the natural moral law written by God in their hearts, the Lord will not fail to run to their aid and save them at the hour of death. This truth, however, must not dampen the missionary ardor kindled by Jesus on earth: «go and preach the Gospel to every creature». Who can ever calculate the advantage of those who have the grace to live united to Jesus and to his immaculate Bride and the disadvantage of being outside her? «I came to cast fire upon the earth and what do I want but that this fire of truth, of love and of peace be kindled more and more?» (Lk 12:49).

Not for nothing is the Church a «mystery» and the study of her characteristics occupies one of the most evocative treatises of Theology.

Tuesday

Tr. pp. 66-67, «Faith: loving adherence… motherhood of Mary most holy»

Faith makes us believe firmly in the word of God, of which Abraham (Gen 15:6) gave heroic proof, ready for the gravest of sacrifices, fully abandoned to the infinite merciful goodness of God.

No less is the full trusting abandonment to God on the part of Moses on so many occasions during the long and suffering pilgrimage toward the promised land. His faith is such that it turns into full confidence to the point of stopping the threats of God, justly angered by the many infidelities of the people. This faith, resting entirely on the promise of the future Redeemer, constitutes the prelude to Christian faith, not only in Jesus Christ as Messiah, but essentially as God, identical with the Father under the veils of human flesh, as today under the veils of bread and wine.

The key point of Christian faith is, therefore, to believe in the divinity of Christ proclaimed in the Prologue of his Gospel by John and explicitly confirmed by Jesus himself more than once «before Abraham was, I am» (Jn 8:58).

The clear testimony of his divinity will in fact be the determining reason for his condemnation to death by crucifixion. To the high priest who asks him: «I adjure you by the living God to tell us whether you are the Christ, the Son of God», Jesus answers: «You have said so». Then Caiaphas tears his garments, saying: «He has blasphemed! What further need have we of witnesses?». And the Sanhedrin decrees: «He deserves death» (Mt 26:62ff.). Jesus openly testifies to his divinity. Before this testimony the death sentence follows immediately: «He said he was the Son of God. We need no witnesses». Those present were all witnesses of what he testified of himself, but only someone truly just and sincere, like Nicodemus, will become his follower.

The first and principal truth of faith is therefore the divinity of Christ, from which all the others spring: faith in the most holy Trinity, the truth of all the mysteries of Christ: resurrection, ascension, descent of the Holy Spirit, including the divine motherhood of Mary most holy.

Wednesday

D. pp. 103-104, «The Spirit who bursts into her… in the image of Christ and of Mary»

The Spirit who bursts into her as «fire» is in Rosa's mystical experience a constant that illumines, bringing out the centrality of Love in her relationship with the third Person of the Trinity.

The divine fire evokes various biblical images, expressions of the presence of the Spirit in individual persons and in the community: «John is that Elijah who is to come, the fire of the Spirit dwells in him and makes him run before the Lord who comes»; «…on the day of Pentecost… there appeared to them tongues as of fire, which parted and rested on each one of them, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit…» (Acts 2:1ff). Rosa too mystically experiences the Spirit Love, Fire dwelling in her, and attests its modalities in the pages of her spiritual memoirs:

«Oh! you are too sweet…; alas, a fire consumes me… it is… as if I had a furnace»;

«For several days the region of my heart seems to want to open… the fire is burning…»;

«…the fire grew in me more and more so much that I could not stand on my feet…»;

«…I thought I would die from the fire; the union with my God devoured me so that I had to distract myself lest they notice…»;

«The fire devoured me, a something on the left side I felt that everything within me moved and this sweetest movement when it comes upon me makes me die…» (M. 1.1, p. 120; M. 12, pp. 31; 46; M. 3, pp. 1; 23).

The gift of the Father, the Holy Spirit, did not exhaust his mission in Mary, burning bush of the definitive theophany, full of grace, in whom with the power of his love he formed Jesus. He continued to be the Love, the power of life, of the mission and resurrection of Jesus, and continues in every human being to transmit the Trinitarian life and to form in him a child of God.

Within the horizon of this his mission of love is placed his action in regard to Rosa, in whom he «dwells» making himself mystically experienced as fire and molding her with this fire in the image of Christ and of Mary.

Thursday

FS pp. 263-265, «Deeply convinced… or a paralyzing legalism»

Deeply convinced, as she is, that everything is the work of God, it is natural for her to attribute to Him every good outcome of the presence and action of the Daughters of St. Anne and the rapid expansion of the Institute; on the contrary, each time a difficulty arises or unpleasant news reaches her about the conduct of the sisters, she attributes it to her own incapacity or her own faults:

«What should I say? only that this happens because of me: behold my sins! Courage, let us trust in God: He, as it is His Work, will provide for everything»

- «Ah! yes, let me say it: this Work, the blows it receives are all the fruit of my infamies. If it so pleases God, let us adore his divine Majesty» (Letter to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 6-8-1870, 16-11-1871).

This same awareness of being herself the real obstacle to the progress of God's Work made her think more than once of resigning and leaving to another the responsibility of the general government. On noting, however, that such a thought assailed her precisely in the moments of great sorrows because of the Work, she suspected that it was suggested to her by the infernal enemy, and then she reacted as against a temptation, as if she wished selfishly to withdraw from the weight of her own mission. On 5 June 1880, on feeling herself accused by the bishop, unjustly, of helping her own children with the goods of the Institute, she wrote:

«I suffer immensely… I do not say what the enemy is suggesting to me; ah! he takes advantage, and thus torments me immensely. He goes so far as to say to me: «For you there will be no more peace… Then I keep studying how I can manage to be put out of this office; I study it and this almost comforts me, when in my mind I find a means that seems to me the one that could help me to be removed and put in some lowly office. But I no longer pray this. It is true that I see the traitor who immediately seems to say: I have won!…» (M 4.5, pp. 196-205).

Mother Rosa's charismatic awareness had a clarification and, I would say, a progressive growth. Without her realizing it, God made her mature through a series of liberations from the conditionings that successively prevented her from collaborating fully with the divine plan, in the originality of her own evangelical line.

God led her to leave her Genoa to free her, not only from the closeness of her own family and relatives, but also from the social and religious commitments that bound her to the works and associations of which she had become the soul.

In Piacenza she felt freed and available for the work of God. But here too she will have to untie herself from new conditionings that can divert the purpose of the Institute or at least hinder its spiritual and apostolic impetus, shutting it up in the narrowness of a vigorless asceticism or of a paralyzing legalism.

Friday

FS p. 139, «She declares herself several times… then her cry is: Love, how strong you are!»

She declares herself several times a slave for love of her beloved Good. There is no lack of painful absences, in which she feels as if forgotten, unworthy even of a glance from the God of Love; but suddenly she feels him near, sweetly drawn by Him, and hears in her depths his voice that reassures her of his love and says to her: «You are my favorite» (M 4.4, p. 76f).

When she experiences such assurance, everything becomes easy for her, every pain desirable:

«Your love, my Good, surpasses all things and is the support, the relief, the security of action. It is the anchor that it casts into the depths of the painful sea of our tribulations. Most lovable God, when in the midst of such sad suffering you leave us anchored in your love, it is enough to say to the pains: You are sweet, O my beloved! And to the fear of having displeased you follows the confidence of your pardon, the assurance of soon having clarifications in the rest of our actions and, finally, the blessedness of your perfect union which, by means of love, is always savored, albeit in greater or lesser intimacy» (M 4.2, p. 89).

Frequently she finds herself unable to declare the ineffable experiences of infused love. At other times she feels as if invaded, overcome, subdued under the sweet violence of Love. And then her cry is: Love, how strong you are!

Saturday

D. pp. 93-94, «The mention of the Chalice… children who form the Body of Christ, the Church»

The mention of the «Chalice» - «in that Chalice», «I saw myself in a chalice» - brought alongside the words of Paul: «Whenever you drink this cup…»

(1 Cor 11:26) and with the term «blood»: «I saw in the Host the most precious blood», evokes the words of Jesus: «…this is my blood of the covenant… poured out for many». Words that refer back to the 4th song of the Servant of the Lord: «He bore the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors» (Is 53:12).

These references affirm that the Eucharist is the new Covenant inasmuch as it is the definitive and irrevocable gift of God in Jesus Christ for us. It communicates to us, through the gift of the Spirit of Jesus, such a self-giving of Jesus that makes us capable of living and dying as He lived and died.

In the Eucharist, then, is fulfilled in a sublime way the whole Old Testament history of God's Covenants with his people: from the Eucharist is born the new people, the new children who form the Body of Christ, the

Church.

16th Sunday in Ordinary Time

D. pp. 125-126, «In the Church to proclaim… is confirmed to Rosa»

Through the contemplation of the divine mysteries and the listening to the Voice, which in her interior formulates a precise desire of the Father:

«Increase of the Faith».

Rosa experiences the dynamism that the Spirit imparts to the Church and to each of its members so that the purpose for which the world was created may be fulfilled. The Father, in fact, created it with a view to the Church and to communion with his divine life, a communion that is realized through the proclamation and acceptance of salvation. As Jesus began his Church by preaching the Good News, the coming of the Kingdom of God promised for centuries in the Scriptures, so Rosa, keeping alive the words suggested to her in secret: «Increase of the Faith», gathers her strength to give herself to the cause of her Good.

A living member of the Church, «branch united to the vine», she sacrifices herself with love and for love to the Father's plan. The support for making the gift of herself to her God Rosa finds in the Church.

Jesus endowed his Church with a structure: the authority of Peter with the other Apostles, which will remain until the full accomplishment of the Kingdom.

The Apostles, in fact, share in the mission of Jesus, in his power, but also in his lot. Through the authority of the successors of Peter and of the Apostles, the Word of the Father, though sometimes not easy to understand and accept, is confirmed to Rosa.

Monday

Tr. pp. 144-145, «Holiness, the work of divine love… all that exists»

The Holy Spirit nourishes in us the hope of being freed from the slavery of corruption and from the fear of sin «to enter into the freedom of the glory of the children of God» (Rom 8:21).

Yes, the Holy Spirit guides us to freedom, to the whole truth, to holiness. The whole truth is Jesus: «I am the way, the truth and the life». The Holy Spirit, who works without pause, continues his descent into souls: on the day of Pentecost upon Mary most holy and the apostles in a sensible and thunderous way; since then in a gentle and silent way, to imprint on those who thirst for the love of God and for holiness the seal of the seven gifts: Wisdom, Understanding, Counsel, Fortitude, Knowledge, Piety, Fear of God, understood as fear of offending his love, fear of not responding generously to his aspirations.

The Holy Spirit continues always to work in persons, producing in them his fruits: «love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control; against such things there is no law» (Gal 5:22-23).

Pentecost, therefore, has not ended, it continues in souls where it finds the assurance of hope, the insatiable thirst for perfection, the serious will to grow in that charity of which Saint Paul speaks (cf. 1 Cor 13:1ff.). At this point one would say that everything on the path of holiness is the work of the Holy Spirit.

But everything is also the work of the Father: We have not received the spirit of servile fear of the slave, but the spirit of adoption of children in which we cry: Abba, Father! The Holy Spirit himself bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God (cf. Rom 8:15).

Therefore everything is also owed to the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. From his divine fatherhood all «fatherhood and all earthly human motherhood takes its origin and meaning» (Eph 3:15).

Not for nothing does Jesus speak continually of the Father, to such a degree that one day the Apostle Philip says to him: «Lord, show us the Father and it is enough for us». And Jesus answers him: «Have I been with you so long, and yet you do not know me, Philip? He who has seen me has seen the Father. Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in me?» (cf. Jn 14:8-10).

Therefore everything depends on the Father, everything depends on the Holy Spirit. It is no less true, however, that everything depends on the Son: «All things were made through him, and without him was not anything made that was made» (Jn 1:3).

Tuesday

Tr. pp. 152-153, «The people of God… holiness Father, Son and Holy Spirit»

«The people of God shares also in Christ's prophetic office, spreading everywhere a living witness to him, especially by means of a life of faith and charity and by offering to God a sacrifice of praise, the fruit of lips that confess his name (Heb 13:15)» (LG 12). The Church, made up of the baptized and of believers, for her part is always holy (as we profess in the Creed) and sanctifying. Even sin, in fact, does not destroy in the sinner the sanctifying effect of baptism: seed, root of a possible return to God and of the consequent sanctification.

The holiness of the Church has its icon in Mary most holy Immaculate. And as the Immaculate is the Mother of the Word made man, so the Church, continually, by means of the sacraments generates and regenerates holiness, thanks to her indissoluble union with Christ, her most holy bridegroom, the holy one by essence, the first principle of all holiness: Father, Son and Holy Spirit.

Wednesday

Tr. pp. 159-160, «That Christ may dwell through faith… spiritual and of holiness «

«That Christ may dwell through faith in your hearts, that you, being rooted and grounded in love, may have power to comprehend with all the saints what is the breadth and length and height and depth, and to know the love of Christ which surpasses knowledge, that you may be filled with all the fullness of God. Now to him who by the power at work within us is able to do far more abundantly than all that we ask or think, to him be glory in the Church and in Christ Jesus to all generations, for ever and ever» (Eph 3:14-21).

Into these abysses of God's love Mother Rosa Gattorno entered with firm will and enlightened generosity. In her footsteps the way remains smoothed to reach holiness, both for all the members of her spiritual Family and for those who follow her teaching and example.

Mother Rosa's own charism splendidly facilitates the path toward holiness, the goal of human Christian and religious life.

Mother Rosa entered into the mystery of Christ's charity and advanced admirably to the last degrees of the spiritual life, penetrating the wisdom of the cross, in a manner not unlike the experience of Paul:

«And I, brethren, when I came to you, did not come proclaiming to you the testimony of God in lofty words or wisdom. For I decided to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ and him crucified.

And I was with you in weakness and in much fear and trembling; and my speech and my message were not in plausible words of wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power, that your faith might not rest in the wisdom of men but in the power of God. For the Spirit searches everything, even the depths of God» (cf. 1 Cor 2:1-5.10).

Mother Rosa reached the highest degrees of the mystical life by retracing the way of Calvary: «The Crucified» Jesus, in the mystery of his poverty, was her «Good».

This is the surest way of spiritual progress and of holiness.

Thursday

Tr. pp. 142-144, par. 1.4

Docility to the action of the Spirit makes us new creatures, transformed into the image of Christ Jesus and ever more aware of living in him, through him and with him the inheritance he has acquired for us by offering himself as victim of the new Covenant.

The Father himself illumines this reality of ours through his Word: «The Holy Spirit bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God. And if children, then heirs, heirs of God and fellow heirs with Christ, provided we suffer with him in order that we may also be glorified with him. For I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worth comparing with the glory that is to be revealed to us» (Rom 8:16-18).

Since we must, therefore, share in the suffering of Christ, and since the Father knows our weakness, he does not leave us alone in the effort of identification with the firstborn Son of every human being.

«The Spirit helps us in our weakness; for we do not know how to pray as we ought, but the Spirit himself intercedes for us with sighs too deep for words. And he who searches hearts knows what is the mind of the Spirit, because the Spirit intercedes for the saints according to the will of God. We know that in everything God works for good with those who love him, who are called according to his purpose. For those whom he foreknew he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, in order that he might be the firstborn among many brethren, and those whom he predestined he also glorified» (Rom 8:28-30).

Mother Rosa believed firmly in God's plan, and therefore did not spare her life, always hoping, even against all hope, in him, her Good, her strength and her defender: «Who shall bring any charge against God's elect? It is God who justifies. Who is to condemn? Christ Jesus, who died, yes, who was raised from the dead, who is at the right hand of God, who indeed intercedes for us. Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword?

As it is written: for your sake we are being killed all the day long; we are regarded as sheep to be slaughtered.

No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us».

This same certainty must grow in us so that we may experience in life, in total surrender to the Father, how «neither death, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers, nor height, nor depth, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord» (Rom 8:38-39).

To be children in the Son is our destiny, but it is still the object of our hope. «In this hope we were saved. Now hope that is seen is not hope. For who hopes for what he sees? But if we hope for what we do not see, we wait for it with patience» (Rom 8:24-25).

Friday

Tr. pp. 47-48, par. 2.2

The poverty of Jesus is expressed theologically, according to Saint Paul, in the fact that the Son of God, though he was Lord, creator and king of the universe: «though he was God, emptied himself, took the form and condition of a Servant, assuming human nature in the unity of the divine Person of the Word». He becomes «servant»! Human nature, then, compared with the divine is nothing. Though God, absolute fullness of every good and of every perfection, uniting to himself, personally, human nature, he lowered himself to the poverty of nothingness. He, creator and master of all, made himself poor with the poverty of the servant (cf. Phil 2:7).

This supreme humiliation includes in itself also the poverty of Mary, that of the family of St. Anne and St. Joachim, and the humiliation he accepted by becoming incarnate in the most pure womb of the Immaculate his Mother.

Jesus accepted the straitened circumstances of poverty during the 30 years of hidden and laborious life in Joseph's workshop, working as a carpenter, he lived the poverty of concealment: «Is not this the carpenter's son?» (Mt 13:55), and also in the three years of public life he openly declared: «Foxes have the security and warmth of their holes, birds their nests, but the Son of man has nowhere to lay his head!» (Mt 8:20; Lk 9:58). The poverty of Jesus, therefore, has not only an economic meaning, but takes on a profound theological and spiritual meaning: God who becomes a creature taking the form of «servant»; to come close to us God becomes like one of us, with a gesture of infinite love and, finally, lets himself be arrested, condemned to death, scourged, crowned with thorns, crucified and even stripped of everything, dying naked on the cross.

How could one otherwise explain the charism of Mother Rosa Gattorno, most loving of the Crucified, without this theological, ascetical-mystical background that characterizes her life in so impressive a way?

Saturday

FS pp. 247-248, «She sympathizes and teaches… that vocation must be saved»

She sympathizes and teaches how to sympathize with afflicted sisters, she shares their difficulties with expressions of an unspeakable tenderness, but without sentimentality. She writes to one of them:

«Your sorrows I carry with me and I always make of them an offering to God, so that one day they may shine upon your head and with greater glory you may occupy that beautiful place that Jesus has prepared for you. Courage! (Letter to Sr. A. Aquilina Gilardoni: 10-10-1889).

And to another:

«You cannot believe how much it grieves me to see you so afflicted. I do not want it! the tribulations that hurt us most are the sensible ones, but for this reason we must not dwell on them. No! a generous offering to God, and that is all!… Courage, dear daughter, for I take a lively part in your sorrow; but God so permits, that we may detach ourselves from everything and be ever more for Him… Do not fear, for I am always with you!» (Letter to Sr. A. Battistina Bertuzzi: 13-7-1887).

In her letters her concern for the health of individual sisters becomes almost a commonplace. First of all for spiritual health: she experiences real trepidation at the mere thought that someone might be unfaithful to the Lord. Writing to a superior in America about the case of a young professed sister who is in crisis, she orders her to do on her behalf whatever is necessary, transferring her wherever fitting, sparing no journeys: that vocation must be saved (Letter to Sr. A. Aquilina Gilardoni: 29-10-1898).

17th Sunday in Ordinary Time

FS pp. 278-280, «She experiences a special… my Good keeps teaching me»

She experiences a special divine assistance in the heavy work, above all when to the weariness are added spiritual aridity and the other sufferings.

«Dear Monsignor: Tribulations come daily, they never stop, never! one more terrible than the other. I feel crushed and I see my poor body too worn down: the years, the continual journeys, the sufferings and more the terrible torment of my poor spirit buffeted from all sides. I do not know how and where to calm myself. Work! I feel an obligation of conscience that drives me; humanity shrinks back from work, it seems to have lost my energy..»

- «After a long suffering I resolved to depart and begin my old life: it is better to die working than to sell oneself to the cure!» (Letter to Msgr. Granito di Belmonte: 18-6-1888, 2-9-1893).

The same indomitable will to die under the weight of the mission of foundress she expresses in a beautiful paragraph of the circular of 7-12-1895:

«If nothing has been able until now to stop my step for your good and for the greater glory of God, I assure you that, until the last breath of my life, I shall always be the same and shall not fail to come to your aid in any need of yours».

In Mother Rosa's Memoirs there is frequent experiential observation of divine help through that charismatic gift of her own intuition about the situation of persons and of the signs through which God lets her know what is happening in this or that community, what is troubling this or that sister. Almost always these are painful situations that make her suffer and begin to pray, redoubling her penances. Very often she feels that a higher light suggests to her what she must resolve in certain difficult cases concerning the Work (cf. M 4.2, p. 81-84). She writes on 23 February 1875:

«When I have to speak of certain small things, it seems to me that I find them all easily in my mind, others, grave ones of the Work, are so clarified in my mind, everything as if I had to draw them out already prepared. Oh! how I reflect that I did not have the slightest thought in this Work and only had the material task of putting in its place what my Good keeps teaching me!» (M 4.3, p. 28).

Monday

FS pp. 168-169, «For one who loves God… all the great mystics»

For one who loves God, in fact, the evil of evils is sin. Rosa Gattorno wept all her life over what, in her humility, she called «my great sins», «my wickednesses», not because she doubted God's forgiveness, but precisely because she felt herself so lovingly embraced by the mercy of the supreme Love. The mere thought that she could still offend him tortured her atrociously.

It is well known among those versed in spirituality that one of the most effective means of purification is the struggle against temptations, of which the most terrible are those concerning the foundation of faith and trust in God. Sometimes these are true diabolical obsessions, other times simple obscurations that fix themselves tenaciously in the interior faculties in the form of scruples, fears, anguish and despair. The torment of the spirit reaches its height when the soul feels it has lost its God forever, seeing itself irremissibly damned.

God did not spare Rosa Gattorno this price of the victory of Love, common to almost all the great mystics.

Tuesday

TC pp. 136-139, «Oh! it is you… where there is great need: you will find something to do.»

- Oh! it is you whom we have awaited for so long! May you be blessed by God!

- Tell me, who are you?

- A worker who awaits you so that you may give me work. But how many like me there are over there!

- Have they all already begun to work?

None. I tell you that all await you. How did you know that I had to come?

For many years we have desired to be able to serve the Lord by working in his vineyard, but it was never granted us. Many prayers and tears we shed, but nothing! The field we saw beautiful and always flourishing, but greatly in need of being cultivated. Beautiful plants! and many are spoiled at the root. Finally, after so much sighing, a beautiful and graceful shepherd came, who at the mere sight of him left us in ecstasy and, with supernatural manners, announced your coming to us and promised us great things for whoever will be faithful to you in the work. And he vanished.

- Ah! - I cried out - It was my Lord! Tell me where he stopped to speak to you and the ground on which he set his most holy foot.

Oh! how breathlessly I ran to see where my God had been!

- Just a few steps more - the peasant woman began to say - and we are there.

What palpitation, what indescribable joy! This poor girl calmed me and fussed to stop me so that I could catch my breath. Behold! I threw myself on the ground and with all my soul I kissed and kissed again that ground. And then I would have wanted to enclose it in my breast, which was pounding strongly. The poor girl, who still did not understand and whose heart had not yet tasted and experienced the effects of the love of God, looked at me, and then (remained) unmoved, bored, and moreover held little regard. I cared about nothing, but that ground… Here, my Love, you have been! Oh! how strong this thought is! I enclosed that ground well. But no! I must carry this earth with me, which I pressed tightly to my breast. My voice:

- No! no one will be able to tread on this; my angels stand guard over it.

Oh! how painful was the departure for me! I did not insist. As soon as I arrived I found indeed a beautiful and immense graceful field. The workers all around made a great feast for me.

- Tell me, have you all seen my Lord? and heard him spoken of? Oh! how beautiful he is!

- Not all (they answered). They invited me to sit and busied themselves making me observe the beauty of the field. There were fruit trees of every kind and in many of these they made me observe that a small woodworm had crept in around them, which gnawed their pith and they were dying. Other weeds, which stretched long around the vine and took away its sap so that it could not (bear fruit). In almost all the wheat darnel had sprung up. From the sight and together with the account a serious thought seized me: a field so vast, with so great a variety of crops, and so few workers! I leaned back thoughtfully; but my voice:

- Who will do this? you and the workers, or the Master?

I was ashamed and, smiling, I told those dear creatures to set to work. Several of them tell me that they lack tools and that, if I do not provide them, they cannot obey me.

- Without faith! Come with me!

But these sat down. Others, who were the greater number, followed me. Having arrived and given each one her work, behold, they all had most beautiful tools. I see one who had more beautiful ones than the others and I was eager to know the reason, and who had given them to her. Without the others noticing, I draw near her and ask her from whom she received such beautiful tools. With the greatest respect she says to me:

- From you!

- How? - to myself - I did not notice having given them to her.

- With your own hands - she answers.

And I looked at her without saying anything more. I understood the mystery well. Oh! my God! What goodness!

And so, working, in a short time the field was cleaned and all the plants flourishing.

Beautiful is your work, my God!

Those who remained seated we found rotted, dead from idleness!

What a surprise for all! I entrusted all the others to the one who had the most beautiful tools and, with the blessing of my God, I would have wished to remain with them.

My voice: it is time to reap! Go where there is great need: you will find something to do.

Wednesday

Tr. p. 85, «The chosen people… and to increase the love of God»

The chosen people knew the importance of letting themselves be prudently guided by God, by wisdom (cf. Wis 9:11); in doubt over a choice they were called to respect the supreme dominion of God: «With God are counsel and understanding» (Job 12:13). From generation to generation the faithful learned: «Learn prudence, you simple» (Prov 8:5); «wisdom teaches temperance and prudence» (Bar 3:9ff.).

In this school St. Anne and Mary her daughter had been educated, enlightened by that prudence which Jesus, as Teacher, will teach to all humanity.

When he sends his disciples to proclaim the Gospel, he in fact warns them: «I send you out as sheep in the midst of wolves, so be wise as serpents and innocent as doves» (Mt 10:16).

Jesus' warning continues to have all its value today, as it had in the time of Mother Rosa, who lived applying to all her choices the criteria of this virtue without separating it from simplicity.

«Prudence is that light which between two things makes you always choose the one that best leads you to gain and to increase the love of God» (Rule 1869, p. 25).

Thursday

FS pp. 226-228, «Mother Rosa felt… of the services of the Daughters of St. Anne»

Mother Rosa felt compensated for so many bitternesses in the audience granted her by Leo XIII in April 1885: the Pope questioned her at length about the Institute and showed himself very satisfied with what the Daughters of St. Anne were doing. Comforted with the papal blessing, she left that audience «drunk with consolation» (FIOCCHI, II, p. 57f).

The third and last great trial that came to refine even further her fidelity to the hierarchical Church was the apostolic visitation of the Institute, begun on 28 July 1898 by the Benedictine abbot Dom Domenico Serafini by order of the Cardinal Prefect of the Congregation of Bishops and Regulars; it had been motivated by certain unfounded accusations about some administrative irregularities and by the printing of the volume Travails and Comforts, which had been denounced to the Holy Office. When the visitor presented her with his credentials and told her the object of the measure, Mother Rosa could not control her emotion; she said through tears: «I already know that I am good for nothing, that I ruin everything: therefore I resign from now on…». Then, encouraged by Dom Serafini himself, she recovered and collaborated with him with all sincerity (FIOCCHI, II, pp. 179-188; Summ., p. 345). A month later, on 30 August 1898, thanking the community of Piacenza for the tribute on the occasion of her name day, she gave a very beautiful address to the sisters and said, with a clear allusion to the trial she was going through:

«Yes, love the Mother, love her in the holy Church… Daughters, one promise I want from you on this day: that you be faithful to the Institute and to holy Mother Church. No, daughters, let not calumnies, worries, anguish make you fall away from the holy vocation… I too was slandered, despised, ill-treated: and not even the slightest thought came to me against the holy vocation…» (FIOCCHI, II, p. 277f).

Death overtook the foundress while the apostolic visitation was still in progress. The visitor himself, having become a Cardinal, was invited to testify in the informative process of Rome and gave a sincere eulogy of the Institute, which he knew well.

The same attitude of obedience and veneration she observed and wanted observed toward the prelates of the dioceses where the Institute had houses. When it was necessary, for the approval of the Constitutions, it was not difficult for her to gather laudatory letters of recommendation from numerous bishops, satisfied with the life and services of the Daughters of St. Anne.

Friday

FS pp. 224-225, «Let it not be forgotten… that it might be incorporated into his Church»

Let it not be forgotten, however, that, if personal relations with the diocesan bishops and with the supreme Pontiffs Pius IX and Leo XIII were easy and full of consolation, the same cannot be said of the dealings with the Roman dicasteries concerning the insertion of the Institute into the structural framework of the Church. The foundress had to suffer setbacks, misunderstandings, even harsh humiliations, which more than once put her unshakable trust in the hierarchical Church to a hard test. Here is how she expresses herself, in her metaphorical language:

«The boat tied up well, as best I knew how, I sought to bring myself to my Good in his great temple, to his Vicar. Oh! what a surprise! So poorly dressed, a beggar as I was, a poor slave of the Lord, I kissed the foot and the hand of his Vicar. O most humble sovereign! O mercy of God! The Vicar asks me about the little ship, wants it near him and prophesies the future to me. O my Savior! with what vigor I had run to fetch the little boat to bring it where the Vicar wanted! But a stormy sea rises, a contrary wind rages and dashes me upon a rock… After a small struggle my little ship came out more beautiful… Brought to the feet of Peter, I knew how to say nothing else to him except that he should say many things for me to my God: that I was bringing the little boat to the feet of his Vicar, that it might be incorporated into his Church» (TC, pp. 218-220).

Saturday

FS pp. 219-220, «Holy mother Church… that this was the will of God»

The profound sense of Church of Rosa Gattorno would deserve a treatise of its own. It is not only submission to the representatives of the hierarchical Church, but a true ecclesial spirituality inspired by faith and nourished by veneration and love. Raised in a family environment where she had to deal with Freemasons and anticlericals, she had to mature in her youth her fidelity to mother Church, a fidelity that became service and apostolic activity, seeking from the beginning to assure herself of the authenticity of her initiatives through the approval and guidance of the diocesan authority.

It was obedience to the archbishop of Genoa Msgr. Charvaz that made her accept, in 1864, at the insistent request of the Servant of God Fr. Giuseppe Frassinetti, first the presidency of the daughters of Mary and then the office of superior of the nascent Pious Union of the Daughters of Mary Immaculate, the new Ursulines. And it was the same archbishop who verified the genuineness of the divine impulse that drove her to found a new institute and encouraged her to go personally to Pope Pius IX to assure herself, from the lips of the supreme Pastor, that this was the will of God.

18th Sunday in Ordinary Time

Tr. pp. 73-75, «Mary most holy… Mother Rosa to the heights of holiness»

Mary most holy instills in our hearts too a new kind of hope: the certainty that the Holy Spirit is working a «new creation». If the Messiah is the Son of God, hope acquires an absolute certainty. All the prophecies and figures of the ancient Covenant acquire a dazzling light: Mary becomes in the full sense the mother of hope, She who will defeat the assaults that the forces of the underworld will devise to the harm of the Church and of souls seriously determined to follow Jesus Christ to the summit of Calvary, as Mother Rosa did so boldly.

Behold Christian hope! In Mary we have the shield of security of our faith and of our hope.

The daughters of St. Anne, and all the other members of the Family of the holy mother of Mary Immaculate, are charismatically called to live Jesus our Hope, a characteristic that distinguishes their spirit, linking itself in a particular way to the holiness of the mother of the Immaculate. This peculiar aspect of the spirituality of Mother Rosa's charismatic Family marks in an unmistakable way the charism inherited from the Foundress, stamped with the spirituality of waiting lived by the mother of the Immaculate, and conforms it to the authentic classical spirituality of the Catholic Church: «To live the Covenant in Christ Jesus, our hope».

Among the theological virtues the virtue of hope therefore stands out. This accentuation takes nothing from the substance of Christian spirituality of all times and characterizes the charism well. It can be said that the charismatic primacy of Hope is enriched by one more point in comparison with the spirituality of other religious Families, almost as if Mother Rosa's followers wished to superimpose on the waiting for glorious Jesus the pregnant long waiting of the chosen people, lived in all its fullness by St. Anne and her most holy Daughter. The emphasis on the theological virtue of hope implies vigilance, the virtue most strongly inculcated by Jesus: «Stay awake and pray, for at the hour when you least expect it the Son of Man will come»; «Watch and pray» (Mt 25:13). This is the attitude of persons who abhor the great enemy of spiritual progress which is lukewarmness, sloth, and the spiritual sleep that blocks the step of ascent toward the heights of the interior life.

Precisely this vigilant and watchful constancy in prayer led Mother Rosa to the heights of holiness.

Monday

Tr. pp. 120-121, «Wholly dedicated… common search for the face of the Lord»

«Wholly dedicated to the salvation of the world, a divine work that transcends every human strength and every human wisdom, the Sisters [and the Brothers] commit themselves to discovering day by day, in the intimacy of personal and communal dialogue with God, his saving will and to opening themselves to the action of the Spirit in order to become docile instruments of the mercy of the Father».

«Aware of this inestimable spiritual patrimony of Mother Rosa, her daughters and those who follow her and live her message will cultivate prayer, applying themselves each day to the meditation of Sacred Scripture [according to the Constitutions and the statutes of each form of life in which the same charism is lived].

The interiorization of the Word is not possible without the interior silence that allows one to listen to God, who manifests himself as «a still small voice», speaks to the heart and asks his creatures: «Be silent and listen».

Very opportunely and acutely the Constitutions further specify: «To bring about the conditions most favorable to prayer it is indispensable that each one practice an asceticism that develops and strengthens the spiritual integration of his tendencies and the practice of the virtues proper to the Institute so as to make of the community [and of the spiritual family] the place of the common search for the face of the Lord» (Const., n. 49, a,b,c; own Statutes).

Tuesday

Tr. p. 54, par. 3.1

The hope that the people chosen by God in the Old Testament lived in the pact of Covenant, stipulated by God with the Patriarchs, with Moses and the Prophets, was founded on the word of God. Hope, the banner of Mother Rosa's spirituality, is founded on the living and unshakable rock that is Jesus Christ himself.

The people of the new covenant, Church generated by the Holy Spirit on the day of Pentecost, walks in hope, in the expectation of the final glorious manifestation of Christ.

The presence between heaven and earth of an eternal pontiff who is the incarnate Word cannot fail to have repercussions on human beings. Humanity reconformed to His head through redeeming suffering, reconsecrated to the Father by the glory of the Son of Man, constitutes the Church, which is certainly the people of God, but also the new Eve who is born from the side of the new Adam, asleep on the cross in the sleep of a death that conquers death forever.

Wednesday

TC pp. 454-457, «Your suffering is enough… nothing of what they want to do to it»

«Your suffering is enough to put a brake on everything»

What a terrible storm! While I thought I was resting a moment in a little farmhouse, behold, a storm so fierce arises, a quantity of thunder and lightning terrified me. With fury one of these devastates a wall. Where to save myself? The agitation becomes terrible. I see clearly that into the ear of that shepherd, in whom I had placed my hopes, a malignant dragon whispers, and in him a real struggle takes place. How to save from these terrible disasters?

Certain caverns open before me, into which I am allowed to enter. Horrible sight! what did they contain? With both hands I covered my face and wept bitterly with sorrow. A graceful workwoman, already dwelling among the elect souls of heaven, set about comforting me, but it was of no avail. The tumults grew and ever more terrible became the entanglements of that game of Satan, who took much pleasure in it. Furious, he went now this way now that; he seduced the workers by assuring them of their proud future; and the shepherd, his mind bound, wrapped in a black cloud, acted, how? His way of doing was so painful to me that, I must say, my chest tightened and my nerves writhed. Why this? It was the sight of the evil that would come of it to the great field of the Lord.

Thrown to the ground and having made a long prayer, after a not short time I felt a certainty that in nothing would that dragon prevail and the foot of the most holy Virgin would crush it. But still horribly I felt the torment. Run? and where? and how to get out of this labyrinth? There is no escape; one must suffer and resign oneself.

- No! - my voice - here in my field no one will be able to twist a hair of yours. Your suffering is enough to put a brake on everything.

- My God! is this my sorrowful journey acceptable to you?

- Very much so! - my voice.

I felt myself revive and, as if a great weight had been lifted from me, I regained strength and with courage set out for work. Along the way, other sufferings came upon me; but on arriving at the farmhouse I found the workwomen much aged, because it had been many years since I had seen them. At once I felt sadness, but after some time I grew used to it, and even tried to relieve them in their small troubles, because they cannot be called sufferings.

Meanwhile the news that was sent to me was so bad about the farmhouse I had left, they gave me a terrible pain and so fiercely did I feel that they acted on my nerves; and above all my head suffered. Oh! when will it be that you put this diabolical monster in irons? So much uproar it is making in that field!… Surely, my Lord, you will have pity on me and on your workwomen.

What was heard was so horrible that, seized with fright, I screamed at the top of my voice. I called to my aid the souls in purgatory and my two helpers, whom I always found ready; but on this occasion everything was closed; nothing appeared to free me from so fierce a struggle. Wherever I turned my gaze there were horrible phantoms, whose only aim was to oppress me. Horrible turmoil! The workwoman, as if victorious, stayed sure of her deed; but dissembling she bore her part very well; she made herself secure in her strong support. But nothing is secure for one who believes herself strongly defended by man. Oh! how fitting in this case, O my Lord, are your words: Cursed is the man who trusts in man (Jer 17:5); his security will melt like ice in the sun.

These monsters tried to make me feel the most horrible pains; when from afar I see a graceful dove advancing in slow flight; but seeing her fly so slowly it seemed that, instead of coming nearer, she stopped from time to time. What is it? does she halt in the air? Surely she is waiting for something.

Anxious and tired of looking, I almost lost hope that she would still come to me. Might the conflict of the winds carry her elsewhere? I thought of a thousand kinds of things. Then the thought came to me: What can this dove bring me? is it an illusion of mine so far? The dove takes flight and comes directly to me, stopping at my feet. I did not delay an instant in gathering her in my hands; she did not want to lower her wings, but shook them as if to say to me: Look! I lifted the feathers, and in shining words it was written there: My victorious and radiant field will suffer nothing of what they want to do to it.

Thursday

FS pp. 137-139, «O Love,…you are my favorite»

O Love, how strong you are!

Among the bodily phenomena listed above the most frequent, indeed habitual, was that of the fire in the heart, a sensible reflection of what Mother Rosa experienced in her spirit. The most beautiful expressions of her diary are those where she pours out her love before her dear Good. Here is one of the most burning pages, written in 1866 after the rapture, already described, on the feast of All Saints; love and suffering alternate like two impulses of the same never-satisfied longing:

«I found myself near the Side of my Beloved. Oh! what I felt on sensing myself truly drawing near that volcano of love! Oh! how painful life seems to me! O my dear Beloved, ah! let me remain with you and not have to return to this miserable earth! O sorrowful exile! when will you end?

But at once I recovered and said: No! to live in order to suffer! O my dear Beloved! forgive me if I have such thirst to be taken from this valley. But no! - I repeat - to suffer! Exquisite is the honey of your sweetnesses: how not to remain famished? I suffer, and I feel that this miserable one writhes, struggles…; but no, dear Jesus! she will stand firm, with your help, on the cross, suffering and languishing for you…

O my Beloved, your love consumes me; I feel burning in me a devouring flame that burns and consumes me, a continual spasm, which I can no longer bear; but I do not suffer, because, most delightful, the joy I feel is without equal… Satisfy me, for pity's sake, with your love!» (M 1.1, pp. 42-44).

She declares herself several times a slave for love of her beloved Good. There is no lack of painful absences, in which she feels as if forgotten, unworthy even of a glance from the God of Love; but suddenly she feels him near, sweetly drawn by Him, and hears in her depths his voice that reassures her of his love and says to her: «You are my favorite» (M 4.4, p. 76f).

Friday

FS pp. 150-151, «Carrying the cross with Jesus…on the delightful bed of the cross»

The suffering of the Christian, according to Jesus' invitation (Mt 10:38; Lk 9:23; 14:27) and the theology of Saint Paul (Gal 2:19; 6:14), has a name: the Cross. And it is the name preferred by Mother Rosa. She confesses that still in 1859, made greedy by the great consolations of those beginnings, she was not accustomed to «fight under the banner of the holy Cross, delightful and dear». She was a «beginner» (M 1.1, p. 4). But she did not delay in entering fully into the school of the Cross: this will always be her «companion», her «bed of rest» (M 3, p. 25). One day when she was full of bitterness, holding the cross very tightly, she spoke thus with it: «Is it true, my treasure, that you are always my companion?». And she heard a voice that comforted her: «Only from the Cross does one learn to love!» (TC, p. 329).

Not content with constantly having the image of the Crucified before the eyes of body and spirit, she wished to make her love tangible by binding a small cross tightly to her breast, taking her brief rest lying on a cross and often remaining hanging on a large wooden cross she had in her little room in Piacenza. But it was the very mystery of the Cross, more than its materiality, that had shaped her life.

And she would have wanted each of the daughters of St. Anne to become a true lover of the Cross. Encouragements in this sense are very frequent in her letters; here are some:

«Courage on the way of Calvary, if you wish to arrive at being crucified with your Beloved and to die with Him on the delightful bed of the Cross»

Saturday

TC pp. 366-367, «It is I who guide your steps…calmly I fell asleep»

«It is I who guide your steps» - My Good: your words are unchangeable!

My voice:

- Leave her to the direction of the field and go elsewhere: there you will find a good and zealous shepherd who will hand over his flock to you.

I set out, and to myself I kept repeating: where can it be? why, dear voice, do you not tell me where this shepherd is to be found? while you have such kindness in teaching me, do you send me thus groping? How much pain I feel from the fear of making a mistake! My voice:

- This cannot be, because it is I who guide your steps!

At this answer I prostrated myself on the ground and, with arms open in the sign of the cross, I gave thanks to the Most High. I began to recite the prayer of the most holy Virgin and quicker than ever I hastened my step. Arrived at the foot of a crag, there was no longer any way to go forward. I would have climbed if I could have scrambled up, but I had to stop without moving. I did not complain nor think where I was: nothing! I sat down and quite joyful (I said):

- My Good, your words are unchangeable!

I was full of faith that my God would in an instant have turned that mountain into a royal and delightful plain. Night comes; the torrent that divides the road from the mountain swells: and nothing! I begin to feel an uproar.

Ever steady, I took a few stones and made of them as best I could a seat. It grew ever darker. With my Crucifix clasped to my breast, calmly I fell asleep.

19th Sunday in Ordinary Time

TC pp. 295-298, «Love, for you are loved!…to remain until the last breath»

She weeps bitterly over a curiosity - love, for you are loved.

Recovered, my God! I was no longer in the temple, but in an immense field, which was uncultivated and had to be set right and put in order. I called some good workwomen and as best as possible it could be set right. But there was another, all wheat, but in it there was much couch grass. In fact, it was so intermingled that it could not have strength even to hold up the little ear. Without thinking of the size of the field, I set to work with all the strength I had; I pulled up that malignant weed and had already made a large heap. It crossed my mind: who will carry it away? My voice:

- There is one who thinks of that: work!

And ever more I pulled up. Glancing at the wheat, I see it more luxuriant, and the more it grew and grew strong, the more my strength grew together with courage. When I see two young men of such graceful manners arrive with a cart and carry away the couch grass, and as the heap was large they removed it for me; but I could not see where they took it. Curiosity seized me to approach them and ask. Overcome by it, I stopped pulling up the couch grass and approached them; I asked them what they did with it and where they took it. They answered me in a sad tone:

- Your curiosity, scattered over the worked wheat, the very same, look at it: it burns!

I leave off describing the sorrow, the anguish: it is better to consider it than to describe it. With my face to the ground, I implored them to ask pardon for me from my God. I took hold of a trunk all thorns and beat myself so much that I shed copious blood. What to do? I am lost! I have displeased my God; I do not deserve, no, pardon! And they looked at me.

Such exhaustion seized me that I fell and was about to lose my senses, when one of them, taking me by the hand, (said to me):

- You are forgiven!

I look: it was a very beautiful angel. Full of shame I continued to weep and thank God, telling him that he too should thank him, with lively promises that I would never again commit acts of curiosity.

- Look! - he said to me - The wheat is once more beautiful and healthy after you have worked it.

The devil whispered to me to ask him where the other had gone who together with him carried away the bad weed. Oh my Love! - I exclaimed loudly - it will never be!

The angel, noticing my fear and languor, because I remained exhausted, to test my obedience and to do something pleasing to my God, told me to hurry by going to pull up the other couch grass and to clean the field. I rose without uttering a word, quite content to bring (the work) to an end. But I fell. With courage and lively desire to go there, I rose; but again I fell. My God! a little strength! I do not deserve it, but this body will not stand up. And I tried to help myself as much as I could in order to manage to walk. My efforts were useless. My angel comes up to me and, taking me by the hand, (says to me):

- With your blind obedience, with the love of carrying out God's orders, you have gained much, and the strength you desire the Lord grants you entirely.

It was a second! And I, strong as a giant, cleaned the fields. And I set off on my path, running full of ardor for the glory of God and to seek in everything his will.

I reasoned about the matter and deeply felt lively sorrow. My voice:

- Enough! you must forget: love, for you are loved!

Oh! sweet Love! how to arrive at being able to do something pleasing to your being? Having said this, rapt, I do not know whether I walked with my feet on the ground or rather, I would say, as I believe, I flew. In an Eden of Paradise I was startled: everything spoke to me of love! It was an enchantment, my Love! my bones, the marrow of them were being consumed in me: Love! A soft and melodious song I heard, which likewise added to my destruction. Every so often I could say nothing else: My Love! I die! But sweet it would be to be consumed with love and to die of love! go on! continue, O sweet sounds! your echo destroys me. My Love, here let me remain until the last breath!

Monday

TC pp. 49-51, «The victorious Crucified…but the strength of the Crucified prevailed.»

Year 1890, December 28.

My Crucified! along a road he led me and on it I fell ill. He was my physician; in weariness he gave me strength; many times I slipped on the narrow path, and He held me up so that I would not fall and plunge to the bottom of the cliffs.

My Crucified! I fell asleep numb with cold, and He warmed me so that I would not remain buried in lukewarmness.

My Crucified! I was very deformed, and with his grace he made me beautiful, adorning me with his graces; he stripped me of the old man and of a gentle creature I remained clothed.

My Crucified! He taught me to suffer and, like the honey of bees, shut up in those precious nests of wax, he preserved suffering for me: this was changed into sweetness. Now and then he gave me some of this humor to taste, and with sublime lessons made me understand how such exquisiteness was drawn from suffering, while nature was rebellious.

My Crucified subdues humanity, gives vigor, energy and strength to the spirit which, victorious, rules over all the faculties, and so well are they subject; self-love is dissipated and vanishes, is lost and even one's own name is forgotten. Pride is conquered and as an instrument of disdain is looked upon, as an enemy. One feels much pleasure when one sees them crushed and oppressed. Great consolation is felt by the will, which is overbearing; and this my Crucified has exchanged for His own! It is sweet, infinitely pleasant no longer to possess it. Oh! how it would have rebelled if He had not nailed it!

My Crucified! He took away my taste, and so, mortified in all foods and gluttony chastised, I had to struggle, but the strength of the Crucified prevailed.

Tuesday

FS pp. 187-188, «At certain moments she resorted…my eternal All»

At certain moments she resorted to penances to give vent to love and also to counterbalance the sufferings of the spirit (cf. M 4.5, p. 59); or simply to satisfy her insatiable thirst for suffering. Often her penances have as their aim to give efficacy to the prayer of petition for her own needs, for the needs of others, for sinners, for the souls in purgatory, for the Church (M 1.2, p. 118). But the relation to the life and passion of the Redeemer always returns; from each of her sufferings she takes occasion to mortify taste and every satisfaction, as also to invent new forms of penance. She would have wished to make of her body a true image of that of the beloved Crucified.

From time to time she felt the need to give a purpose to her penances, precisely to avoid the danger of considering them as ends in themselves. One day in 1872 it was the Lord, her «director», who indicated to her with what intention she should practice some of them: «fasting for the conversion of sinners, eating herbs for the providence of the Institute, the chains so that, chained, held close to your Heart and to your love, I may consume the wounds that I bear from them, and they may help me to arrive soon at the most perfect union with you, O my eternal All» (M 3, p. 26).

Wednesday

FS pp. 144-145, «On the contrary… models and architects of such union»

On the contrary, she feels lively remorse whenever she realizes she has not been charitable toward someone in speaking of her before the others:

«I had a sweet reproach from my Good within, because in these days I let slip from my mouth that a sister was so rough, and before several sisters. In saying it, it seemed to me that my aim was upright, to rouse them and make them become quick, so that they might do good; but unfortunately my Good reproached me, and I made a lively promise and with the most intense sorrow wept over the fault. Oh! how it did me good to see the defect I had committed! - Charity! - he repeated to me - While you were saying that: Charity! My Jesus what pain! Ah! for pity's sake, forgive me! He made me see the ugliness of this imperfection» (M 4.4, p. 93f).

If the love of God was the topic that most fired her when she spoke to the sisters, that of fraternal charity was the most frequent, indeed one may say it was the fulcrum of her pedagogy. And it is not a matter of fine reflections on the queen of virtues: Mother Rosa wanted mutual love to manifest itself in the concrete attitudes of daily life, in reciprocal attentions, in solicitous collaboration, in knowing how to overcome selfishness, misunderstandings, murmurings and the other enemies of fraternal living. Especially the superiors were to be models and architects of such union.

Thursday

TC pp. 255-257, «To the aid of the workwomen…he has prepared a great work for you»

Meanwhile a person comes up to me and invites me to go with her to a field where all the workwomen were in disarray:

«Run to restore order! They no longer listen to the overseer, indeed they mock her and each one thinks of doing as she pleases.»

I look to see whether I see my way. No!

«Who, please, are you?»

«One of those of the field in disarray.»

«But I can do nothing for you, because your flock does not belong to me, being a wretched slave who cannot go where my Master does not send me. You must go and look for some good shepherd who will come to put that flock in order.

She insisted so much; but I stood firm, because I saw no path at all. In the end, with good manners, I tried as much as I could to dismiss her. What does this unhappy one do? She digs in her heels and, resolute, (says to me):

«If you do not come, I stay right here!»

«My God! How can you so resolutely stay, when I do not know you at all?»

My voice:

- Stop her! If she goes back she perishes.

What pain! I stopped her; but she wept for her companions who were about to be devoured by certain evildoers: it was because of these that the confusion had arisen. And then,

- Go - she added - for pity's sake!

My path was not visible, the voice told me nothing and I felt a strong sorrow. She continued the story; from time to time I ordered her to be silent, because I suffered too much. At last (I said to her):

- Why do you not have a shepherd?

- Oh! there was one but, poor man, he had to withdraw, because he could not manage us; seeing that he could do nothing, he went away.

- So you are alone? Do you not even have the guide?
