- Oh! - with a deep sigh - alas we have her, but this evil has all come from her, who first threw everything into disorder.

How I felt myself torn apart! But I saw nothing that indicated I should take charge of it. What did I do? I invited her to join me and, prostrate on the ground, we made lively supplications to the Most High, that he would free those poor workwomen. But I never felt anything that they would be freed. It was real grief; I wept over it and that poor girl did the same: it was agony to see her.

- My Lord, my Master, my God! be moved to compassion for them and for this poor creature who, moved by sorrow at the loss of her companions, weeping begs you to have pity and mercy on them.

This said, a great din is heard. They were those unhappy ones who, in a frightening way, came seeking help, because frightened or, better to say, touched by divine grace, they fled from the lions to throw themselves into the arms of that God whom they had so outraged. I welcomed them as kindly as I could and their poor companion did the same. I gave them a glance to see whether I could recognize the guide among them, but it was not granted me. Perhaps I am mistaken (I said to myself), but there is no certainty. With this thought I went up to the first and asked her. Oh unhappy one! she had gone off with the lions, taking another with her. I tried to restore them; and then I handed them over to my keeper that she might keep them well and try to remove their evil ideas, and finally lead them and set them on the right path. While everything remained in order, my voice:

- The path is traced: run swiftly where the Master has prepared a great work for you.

Friday

TC pp. 448-450, «The true sweetnesses…where my voice indicated to me»

Night was drawing near. My God, what agitation! by how many fears I felt oppressed! When I hear a murmur; and I could hardly make out that it was the chatter of women. Behold them all festive coming up to me, inviting me to go together with them. I did not answer at once. I asked them where they came from and who they were. They answered me that they desired nothing else but the good of creatures and that they helped many.

- Come - they repeated to me - and you will be happy.

- Tell me: in what does your happiness consist?

They stop:

- Why do you ask us so?

- You speak to me of happiness of this world, where all is weeping and sorrow?

- What talk is this? We are happy and in our revelries we feel great pleasure.

- And does the world have many delights to give you? - I continued.

- Perhaps you are an anchorite and do not know these delights; but if you come with us we will let you taste them.

I looked at them closely, and then began to weep:

- Oh! unfortunate creatures! Your deceptive delights last little, and then?… Oh! the true sweetnesses can be had only in God!

They laugh at this speech of mine. But I, having dried my tears, began to describe to them the sweetnesses of religious life: how God prepares for whoever serves and loves him an eternity of good. Noticing that they no longer laughed and listened to me with attention, what eagerness I felt in myself! I would have wanted in a word to make them understand everything.

Night was drawing near, but they begged me to remain in that field, in order to continue my account. So it was. All night was spent always speaking of God and of his Bride the Church. I was able to learn that these were eight young women who, having fled their fathers' houses, wanted to go and throw themselves into the darkest whirlwind of the loathsome world. In the end, enamored of the delights of the Creator, they promised me to leave everything and come with me to cling to the dear Crucified and to give heart and affections to Him alone.

They said to me:

- We have never heard of these things. Mother and father spoke to us of nothing but the world and of what was beautiful in it.

- Oh! poor creatures! how unhappy you have been! Unfortunate parents, what a dreadful account they will have to render to God!

Having reassured them well and given them to a good overseer, I went off where my voice indicated to me».

Saturday

TC pp. 268-271, «She finds mute children…and mute I walked the road»

Only on recovering did I find myself in a delightful garden, where there were a few children. I asked them who they were and whose that so beautiful place was. They did not answer me. Perhaps they are mute? And I tried to make myself understood by signs. I was not mistaken: they were poor abandoned creatures, who sought refuge. How much compassion they aroused in me! I took them with me, because they had knocked a great deal at that palace, but no one had listened to them. All joyful they skipped around me. I thought at once that they were hungry. Turning to my God: what can I give these creatures, who have nothing? what must I do? Having taken off my cloak and approaching a woman who had much bread, I begged her to accept my cloak and give me bread for these creatures I found along this road. The good woman looked at me and, taking the cloak, gave me plenty of bread. This distributed to the poor creatures, I looked for where I could find a brook to give them to drink; I see in the distance a little girl with an amphora who was heading toward us. Oh! what pleasure I felt (and they) no less than mine. I noticed that these poor creatures were burning with thirst and rejoiced to be able to have water. Who sends you, dear creature? As soon as she was near us, she sets down her amphora and invites us to drink. However many questions I put to her, I could never understand who had sent her and who she was. She took back her vessel and, with extraordinary speed, flew away, because more than walking one can say (it was) flying.

These poor creatures were tired, and where to make them rest? My voice:

- A few steps more and you will find shelter for these creatures. So it happened. To an old woman, sitting on a stone, I asked whether she would do me the charity of lodging these creatures. Grumbling she looks at me:

- I have only one bed and this is for me!

- Tell me, do you not have straw?

Unwillingly she points out a hayloft to me, which I accepted at once. And as best I could I put these creatures to sleep. But, once they were asleep, I set myself to pray and weep: what shall I give these poor little ones tomorrow? My God, I feel torn apart!

As soon as (day had broken), I went to the woman, who was already grumbling around the hearth. I begged her to be willing to give me bread for the poor little ones who were sleeping. What did I do? I took off my skirts and gave them to her, so that she would give me bread. She became cheerful, accepted the skirts and gave me plenty of bread and fruit. How happy I was! I looked at the basket with great satisfaction; those poor creatures came to meet me skipping and at once I put the basket at their disposal and they ate their fill. The rest I took and we set off along the path.

How shall I be able to teach these mute creatures to love God and make him known to them? Thinking thus, I looked at them and felt great compassion. I heard a bell, and the more we ran the nearer we came to it. It was a pretty little village with civilized people; I asked a young woman where the church was:

- I hear ringing and I do not understand where the temple is.

She told me that there are certain good souls who have the mute girls. I cannot express what I felt! Arrived at these, I begged them to accept the poor little ones I had with me. They did not delay in granting my request; but the sorrow on both sides at having to part was something…! But they must learn to know God! My voice:

- One day you will see them again. On Calvary Jesus is found! And mute I walked the road.

20th Sunday in Ordinary Time

TC pp. 523-524, «Symbolic vision… he gave me a glance and everything vanished»

Symbolic vision of the suffering Church: My God, accept me as victim!

Sad I moved my step, seized by the thought that on this earth nothing was worthy of a God. Why this profound thought? Is it not You, O Creator, who took delight in creating everything that exists?

I raise my eyes to heaven: what do I see? Seven tablets reddened with blood, which seemed supported by streaks of fire; a most beautiful angel, much like Saint Michael, held them up with a long vine-shoot. From afar, Peter, head of the Church, who was praying, looking at the tablets grew gloomy, and wept. A legion of angels, who sang a sad song, accompanied with their instruments. All was sad.

All stop. In a great and infinite space, almost dark, beautiful souls clothed in mourning were seen. Here and there black cloths were seen. An infinity of people: they stood indifferent, as if susceptible of understanding nothing. Now and then a loud groan came forth: from where? - I said to myself - I look at Saint Peter: it was not he who sent forth such a lament: no! What a lament! it was heartrending. I asked the angel to explain to me what it meant. He answered me:

- It is the Church that suffers!

- The tablets that you hold up, what do they mean?

- I cannot tell you.

He made me see a horrible thing, and said to me:

- This is a most acute sorrow that the Church suffers.

At that sight I felt myself die: such was the dread. It was the indifference of Catholics! It seemed that each one planted in a Heart like sharp stilettos. How to make reparation for this? My God! accept this your slave who offers herself as victim in reparation! I felt nothing. Turning to the angel, I said to him:

- Ah! take such a sight from me and obtain that God accept me as victim of expiation.

I would have wanted to repair everything, but I could no longer bear such a sight. Pity, my God! I saw nothing more: only the tablets and the angel.

- Tell me, what do they mean? Ever more they grew reddened with blood. The angel gave me a glance, and everything vanished.

Monday

FS p. 144, «In the midst of the setbacks…on seeing a soul relieved»

In the midst of the setbacks she had to experience as foundress, she found comfort in this maternal solicitude. She wrote in 1878:

«Recovered from sorrow, nothing is desired, nothing seems that there could be sweet on earth, nothing! Only one thing (the soul) feels it tastes: it is charity. Oh! how much joy it feels in being able to do good and to try to set right, to reconcile in peace with God one who is off the way! Yes, in charity the soul rejoices in everything, takes part in it and, on seeing the well-being of creatures, feels great pleasure. The sacrifice, whatever pain it cost, always turns out a consolation on seeing a soul relieved» (M 1.2, p. 110).
